jobs.title: Principal Program Manager, Strategic Planning & Transformation
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

Job Summary
The Principal Program Manager, Strategic Planning & Transformation role is responsible for shaping, operationalizing, and driving Enterprise Applications strategy. This leader partners closely with senior executives and cross-functional teams to translate strategic priorities into actionable roadmaps, measurable outcomes, and sustained business impact. The role blends strategic planning, execution rigor, financial stewardship, vendor management, and change leadership across complex, matrixed environments.

Key Responsibilities
Strategy Development & Alignment
- Lead development of multi-year strategic plans aligned to enterprise priorities, operating models, and financial targets.
- Translate strategy into clear goals, success metrics, and execution roadmaps across portfolios and teams.
- Assess internal and external trends, risks, and opportunities to inform strategic decision-making.
- Develop business cases, investment strategies, and financial models to evaluate strategic opportunities, prioritize initiatives, and optimize resource allocation.

Execution & Portfolio Leadership
- Drive execution of strategic initiatives, ensuring alignment across business, technology, finance, and operations.
- Establish governance, prioritization, and performance tracking for strategic programs and investments.
- Identify dependencies, risks, and tradeoffs; recommend mitigation strategies to senior leadership.
- Partner closely with Finance to manage strategic investment portfolios, track benefits realization, monitor budgets, and ensure delivery of expected business value.
- Oversee strategic vendor and partner relationships, ensuring contract compliance, performance management, risk mitigation, and alignment to business objectives.

Stakeholder Partnership & Influence
- Act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders, enabling data-driven decisions and alignment across stakeholders.
- Facilitate executive-level discussions, workshops, and planning forums to drive clarity and commitment.
- Communicate strategy and progress in a compelling, concise, and actionable manner.
- Provide executive leadership with recommendations that balance business outcomes, financial performance, operational capacity, and strategic risk.

- Operational Excellence & Change Leadership

- Champion disciplined planning, execution, and continuous improvement practices.
- Drive adoption of new ways of working, operating models, and governance structures.
- Support change management, communications, and capability-building to ensure sustainable outcomes.

Communication & Leadership
- Excellent leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence senior executives and guide large, distributed teams.
- Demonstrated success in stakeholder and vendor management, including contract negotiations, performance oversight, service-level management, and delivery accountability.
- Strong executive presence with the ability to communicate strategic, operational, and financial insights to diverse audiences.
- Proven ability to build alignment, drive consensus, and influence outcomes across a broad set of internal and external stakeholders.

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in Business, Strategy, Engineering, Finance, or a related field (MBA or equivalent preferred).
- 10+ years of experience in strategy, management consulting, transformation, program leadership, or equivalent roles.
- Proven experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives with executive visibility.
- Strong strategic planning, analytical, problem-solving, and financial management skills, including experience developing business cases, managing budgets, forecasting investments, tracking operational spend, and measuring return on investment (ROI).
- Demonstrated financial acumen with experience evaluating investment decisions, portfolio tradeoffs, business value realization, and alignment to organizational financial objectives.
- Demonstrated ability to influence without authority and operate effectively in a matrixed organization.
- Experience managing strategic vendors and partner relationships, including contract governance, performance management, negotiations, and service delivery oversight.

Preferred Qualifications
- Lean Six Sigma Black Belt and PMP or Agile/Scrum certification highly desirable. Other valuable certifications include Lean Six Sigma Green Belt, SAFe, or specific technology/platform certifications (e.g., AWS, Azure).
- Experience in enterprise technology, digital transformation, operating model redesign, or large-scale business transformation.
- Experience managing significant technology, consulting, or managed service vendor relationships and associated budgets.
- Background in healthcare, regulated industries, or large-scale enterprises.

Leadership Competencies
Strategic Thinking: Long-term, enterprise-level perspective with strong business judgment.
Influence & Collaboration: Builds alignment and commitment across diverse stakeholders.
Execution Rigor: Drives results through disciplined planning and follow-through.
Change Leadership: Leads teams through ambiguity and transformation effectively.
Financial & Business Acumen: Demonstrates strong understanding of financial drivers, investment planning, portfolio economics, vendor management, and value realization to support sound business decisions.
Vendor & Partner Leadership: Establishes productive external partnerships, holds vendors accountable to commitments, and maximizes value from strategic investments.

jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Corporate Strategy (Pharmaceutical)
jobs.location: Irving, TX, USA - 6555 North State Highway 161 (P001)
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

This role is a hybrid position. The selected candidate is expected to work on-site at our Las Colinas (Irving, TX) office a minimum of two (2) days per week, with the remaining days worked remotely. Specific in-office days may be designated based on team needs and business priorities.

About the Role:

The Senior Manager, Segment Strategy - Generics is an analytical individual contributor role within the strategy team, supporting the development of frameworks, models, research and strategy recommendations that enable the evaluation and execution of key strategic initiatives for our Generics business within our North America Pharmaceutical Distribution (NAPD) segment. Reporting to the VP, Product Strategy & Strategic Initiatives, this position operates as a key strategic partner to our Generics organization.

Success in this role is defined by the ability to translate complex dynamics into insights, collaborate well across multiple groups / functions, and ensure strategic work leads to practical, executable outcomes.

What You'll Do:

Strategic Analysis & Insight
- Own end-to-end analytical workstreams within larger strategic initiatives — from problem structuring and hypothesis development through analysis and synthesis of findings — with guidance from initiative leads on framing and prioritization.

- Build rigorous fact bases on market structure, competitor strategies and economics, customer segments, and channel dynamics across the pharmaceutical distribution value chain.

- Synthesize complex quantitative and qualitative information into clear, well-structured storylines; consistently deliver the “so what,” not just the analysis.

- Identify implications of your own workstream for the overall initiative, and flag issues and opportunities to initiative leadership proactively.

Value Chain & Financial Analysis
- Build and maintain financial models that translate market shifts — reimbursement changes, sourcing dynamics, customer mix evolution, competitive moves — into quantified P&L implications for the business, with review from senior team members.

- Develop working knowledge of how each participant in the pharmaceutical value chain — manufacturers, distributors, PBMs, payers, and pharmacies — earns, protects, and seeks to expand its economic position.

- Track and analyze legislative, regulatory, and policy developments — including drug pricing reform, PBM transparency requirements, and reimbursement policy changes — and support the assessment of their financial and competitive implications.

- Support scenario and sensitivity analysis: pressure-test the assumptions that matter most and help bound the range of plausible outcomes.

Problem Solving & Collaboration
- Participate actively in team problem solving; step up to lead portions of problem-solving sessions with the team and with business partners.

- Challenge assumptions constructively and take intellectual risks to generate new ideas; bring curiosity about how the distribution business actually works economically.

- Manage your own time and workplan effectively; know how and when to seek input; control the quality of your own work product.

Communication & Stakeholder Support
- Prepare well-written, logical, concise documents and executive materials with minimal guidance; lead with key messages.

- Present analysis and recommendations with confidence to initiative teams and, with preparation, to senior business audiences.

- Build collaborative working relationships with business, finance, sourcing, commercial, and functional partners; project credibility and reliability.

Team & Function Contribution
- Coach newer team members on analytical craft, modeling standards, and story lining; provide constructive upward feedback.

- Contribute to strategy function-building efforts — recruiting, knowledge capture, analytical tooling, and ways of working.

Basic Requirements:
- Degree or equivalent and typically requires 4+ years of relevant experience.

- 4+ years of progressive experience in strategy consulting, corporate strategy, finance, market / business intelligence or comparable analytically intensive roles.

- Exposure to healthcare, generics pharmaceutical services, or distribution businesses strongly preferred; genuine interest in the economics of the pharmaceutical value chain is essential.

- Demonstrated advanced financial modeling capability — building models from a blank sheet that connect market dynamics to P&L outcomes.

- Track record of structuring ambiguous problems, executing rigorous analysis, and producing executive-ready synthesis and deliverables.

- Experience working effectively in cross-functional teams and managing multiple deliverables under time pressure.

Additional Skills/Experience:
- Structured Problem Solver: Formulates clear hypotheses and structures workstreams well with light guidance; handles complex analyses with little oversight and moves efficiently from data to insight.

- Financial Modeling & P&L Literacy: Builds financial models as strategic tools — not to forecast with false precision but to identify the assumptions that matter and quantify the implications of strategic choices.

- Synthesis & Story Lining: Distills complex information into clear, logical storylines; writes and charts at near executive-ready quality; consistently answers “so what.”

- Value Chain Curiosity: Demonstrates genuine intellectual curiosity about how distribution, sourcing, pharmacy, PBM, and payer economics actually work — and is building working fluency in them.

- Collaborative Teammate: Is a reliable, helpful, and proactive teammate; builds trust with partners across the business; coaches junior colleagues and is open to coaching from others.

- Communication: Writes clearly and concisely; presents with confidence in familiar settings; listens well and tailors style and tone to the audience.

Physical Requirements
- General office demands

- Must have the ability to travel up to 20% of the time

- Hybrid: This role will require 2 days per week (Tuesdays and Wednesdays) onsite at our Headquarters in Irving, TX. Non-local candidates will not be considered.

The Sr. Manager, Strategy – Oncology & Multispecialty is an analytical individual contributor role within the strategy team, supporting the development of frameworks, models, and research that enable the evaluation and execution of key strategic initiatives. Initiatives span both commercial segments — provider-facing (GPO, specialty distribution, specialty pharmacy, alternate site infusion, practice management) and biopharma-facing (clinical trial site management, real-world evidence, clinicogenomic data) — and frequently sit at the intersection between the two, where the segment’s most distinctive strategic questions live.

The Sr. Manager will be expected to independently and comprehensively develop an analytical model that supports each initiative and complete required analysis and research required to enable leadership to make informed decisions and develop a path forward. Taking responsibility for accuracy and completeness, the senior manager will be expected to bring their own thoughts and perspectives to the analytical process to ensure effective evaluation of initiatives.

- Participate actively in team problem solving; step up to lead portions of problem-solving sessions with the team and with business partners.

- Prepare well-written, logical, concise documents and executive materials with minimal guidance; lead with key messages.

- Present analysis and recommendations with clarity to initiative teams and, with preparation, to senior business audiences.

- Build collaborative working relationships with business, finance, clinical, and functional partners across both franchises; project credibility and reliability.

jobs.title: Lead Program Manager, Oncology and Multi Specialty Technology Strategy
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

Position Summary

The Lead Program Manager, Oncology and Technology Strategy leads the operational delivery and continued maturation of McKesson's Responsible AI Board (RAIB) governance program within the Oncology and Technology Strategy organization. The role translates Responsible AI policy, RAIB Charter requirements, and business priorities into an executable   program   roadmap, governance structure, operating cadence, service-level expectations, and measurable outcomes.

Partnering with business and technology leaders, Responsible AI Owners, Legal, Compliance, Privacy, Information Security, Architecture, Data, and other control functions, this role manages the full AI Use Case lifecycle across multiple related governance activities. The Lead Program Manager drives cross-functional alignment, manages program-level risks and dependencies, resolves escalated issues, and   maintains   visibility into portfolio health, decision quality, control implementation, and ongoing monitoring.

This is a hands-on program leadership role with accountability for program outcomes rather than only process administration. Success requires the autonomy to lead complex work, influence without direct authority,   establish   scalable standards, challenge inefficient ways of working, and use analytics and automation to strengthen executive decision-making.

Key Responsibilities

Program Leadership and Strategic Alignment

- Break down Responsible AI program   objectives   into measurable business and technology   outcomes, and   maintain a program roadmap that translates governance requirements into executable plans, milestones, deliverables, and success measures.

- Lead the end-to-end AI Use Case governance lifecycle across intake, triage, RAIB Operations quality review, RAIB and EAIC review, final decision, control implementation, and ongoing monitoring.

- Partner with program sponsors and senior stakeholders to align governance priorities, secure support, resolve high-visibility issues, and ensure the program continues to deliver enterprise value.

Governance, Risk, and Dependency Management

- Establish and   maintain   the   program   governance structure, operating cadence, decision rights, escalation paths, service-level   objectives , and delivery standards consistent with McKesson's Responsible AI Program, Responsible AI Policy, and RAIB Charter.

- Identify ,   consolidate , and manage program-level risks, issues, interdependencies, and resource constraints across governance activities; develop mitigation plans, assign accountable owners, and escalate significant risks with recommended actions.

- Lead scope, priority, and   risk   trade-off discussions with stakeholders, driving consensus while preserving policy, control, documentation, and audit requirements.

- Ensure governance records, risk assessments, approvals, conditions, controls, and notifications are complete,   accurate ,   timely , and   audit-ready .

RAIB and EAIC Leadership

- Lead preparation and execution of RAIB sessions and, when   required , EAIC secondary reviews in partnership with the RAIB Operations and Governance Lead and Sr. Product Portfolio Manager.

- Ensure review materials enable informed decisions and that every decision, condition, action, owner, and due date is documented accurately in Smartsheet and communicated within the required response window.

- Serve as the first escalation path for at-risk submissions, unresolved information gaps, missed commitments, or stakeholder conflicts that could affect governance quality, cycle time, or program outcomes.

Stakeholder Leadership and Cross-Functional Collaboration

jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

Role Summary

The Revenue Operations Manager,   NAPD   is responsible for   driving predictable, disciplined revenue execution across a complex distribution sales environment. This role owns pipeline health, forecasting rigor, quota and capacity analytics, and revenue inspection across the NAPD sales lifecycle.

The Revenue Operations Manager partners closely with NAPD Sales Leadership, Finance, Sales Enablement, and Salesforce Product teams to translate Salesforce-enabled selling into consistent execution, trusted forecasts, and decision-ready insights. This role is expected to proactively surface revenue risks, highlight performance drivers, and improve how the organization plans, inspects, and delivers revenue—not simply report on outcomes.

This role offers location flexibility and is open to candidates across the United States.
Candidates based in the Dallas–Fort Worth (DFW) area will be hired in a hybrid capacity. The selected candidate is expected to work on-site at our Las Colinas office a minimum of two (2) days per week, with the remaining days worked remotely. Specific in-office days may be designated based on team needs and business priorities.

Key Responsibilities

Pipeline, Funnel & Deal Health

- Own pipeline health diagnostics and inspection standards across NAPD sales motions, including national accounts and complex manufacturer-aligned opportunities

- Lead recurring Funnel Health Reviews,   identifying   risks related to coverage, conversion, velocity, and deal progression

- Establish and govern funnel hygiene standards to ensure   accurate , reliable inspection in Salesforce

F orecasting & Revenue Confidence

- Drive forecasting accuracy through disciplined inspection, trend analysis, and risk identification

- Provide executive-level pre-reads and insights that clearly articulate forecast confidence, upside, and risk drivers

- Surface early warning indicators tied to pipeline sufficiency, timing risk, and execution gaps

Sales Performance KPIs​

- Establish and govern a clear, consistent set of Sales Performance KPIs aligned to Revenue Operations objectives and NAPD revenue outcomes​

- Define and  maintain  standard KPI definitions, calculation logic, data sources, and inspection thresholds to ensure consistency and trust across Sales, Finance, and Leadership​

- Embed KPI review into regular sales operating rhythms (e.g., weekly funnel reviews, monthly business reviews, quarterly planning) in partnership with Sales Leadership​

- Translate KPI trends and outliers into actionable insights, highlighting execution risks, opportunities, and implications for forecast confidence and revenue delivery

Cross-Functional Partnership

- Partner with NAPD Sales Leadership to support data-driven decision making and execution discipline

- Partner with Business Insights team to define, prioritize, and operationalize Rev Ops dashboards and analytics tools

- Collaborate with Sales Enablement to   identify   coaching opportunities and behavior gaps   impacting   performance

- Align with Finance to reinforce plan-to-quota alignment and revenue confidence

- Provide clear business requirements and feedback to Salesforce Product and   Business Insights   teams to enhance Rev Ops and inspection tooling

Operating Model & Continuous Improvement

- Reinforce a consistent sales operating model across NAPD segments and roles

- Identify   opportunities to simplify, standardize, and improve revenue inspection processes

- Translate complex commercial data into clear, actionable narratives for senior leadership

Minimum Requirement
Degree or equivalent and typically requires 7+ years of relevant experience.

Education

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience

Critical Skills

- 7+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Sales Analytics, or a related commercial function

- Strong experience supporting pipeline management, forecasting, and revenue inspection in a complex B2B environment

- Advanced analytical skills with the ability to synthesize data into actionable insights

Preferred Skills

- Experience in pharmaceutical distribution, healthcare, life sciences, or similarly complex commercial environments

- Experience supporting quota setting, capacity modeling, or coverage planning

- Deep familiarity with Salesforce reporting, dashboards, and inspection workflows

- Strong executive communication skills with the ability to influence across functions

- Comfort   operating   in high-scale, low-margin, high-complexity business models

What Sets You Apart

- You focus on   decisions and execution , not just metrics

- You proactively   identify   risks and opportunities before they surface in results

- You are comfortable challenging assumptions with data

- You thrive in complex, matrixed environments where clarity and discipline matter

Job Description

The McKesson Corporate FP&A team is hiring a Finance Manager (P4) to provide financial planning and analysis support for the Human Resources organization. This role serves as a key finance partner to HR leadership, supporting workforce planning, forecasting, budgeting, organizational initiatives, and executive decision-making across multiple HR functions. The ideal candidate will be located in the Dallas/Fort Worth, TX area; however, candidates near other McKesson HUB locations may also be considered.

Position Description
This role offers an exciting opportunity to join a dynamic and highly visible Corporate FP&A organization. The Finance Manager will serve as a strategic finance partner to HR leadership, providing financial guidance and insights to support business objectives, workforce strategies, and enterprise initiatives.
This individual will lead budgeting, forecasting, month-end close, variance analysis, and long-range planning activities while driving actionable insights that support business decisions. The successful candidate will possess strong analytical capabilities, business acumen, executive presence, and the ability to translate complex financial information into meaningful recommendations for senior leadership.
The ideal candidate will be curious, identify opportunities to improve processes and reporting, influence business outcomes through data-driven insights, and help drive financial discipline across the organization.

- Serve as a finance partner for Human Resources leadership, providing financial guidance and decision support.

- Lead annual operating plan, quarterly forecasts, long-range planning, and monthly financial outlook processes for assigned HR functions.

- Partner with HR leaders to evaluate investments, strategic initiatives, and organizational changes.

Critical Skills
- Strong financial planning and forecasting expertise.

- Advanced financial modeling, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

- Ability to independently manage complex financial analyses and business issues.

- Exceptional business partnership and stakeholder management skills.

- Strong executive communication and presentation abilities.

- Experience developing executive-level reporting and financial recommendations.

- Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including scenario modeling and large dataset management.

- Ability to identify risks, opportunities, and drivers impacting business performance.

- Strong process improvement mindset and continuous focus on automation and efficiency.

- Ability to influence decisions through data and financial insights.

- Demonstrated ability to work independently in a fast-paced and evolving environment.

- Ability to maintain confidentiality of sensitive financial and organizational information.

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience supporting Human Resources, Corporate Functions, or SG&A organizations.

- Experience with workforce planning, compensation, benefits, and organizational expense management.

- Experience with Hyperion Planning, SmartView, SAP, or similar financial planning systems.

- Experience with Power BI or other visualization and reporting tools.

jobs.title: Spécialiste principal(e), Stratégie d’affaires/ Senior Specialist, Business Strategy
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

Sommaire du poste

Le ou la spécialiste principal(e), Stratégie d’affaires est un(e) contributeur(trice) stratégique principal(e) à fort impact, responsable de traduire les priorités de l’entreprise en stratégies d’affaires concrètes, feuilles de route de transformation et initiatives axées sur la création de valeur au sein du réseau de distribution pharmaceutique de McKesson Canada.

En étroite collaboration avec les dirigeants et les intervenants interfonctionnels, cette personne combine réflexion stratégique, rigueur analytique, élaboration de d’analyses de rentabilisation et leadership du changement afin de résoudre des enjeux d’affaires complexes et de soutenir une croissance durable. Le titulaire contribue à orienter la direction stratégique en identifiant des opportunités, en développant des recommandations fondées sur des données probantes et en facilitant une prise de décision éclairée.

Relevant de la Directrice, Stratégie et Activation, ce rôle apporte de la clarté à des enjeux d’affaires complexes, aligne les parties prenantes autour d’une vision commune et contribue à l’atteinte de résultats mesurables soutenant l’évolution à long terme des capacités de la chaîne logistique de McKesson Canada.

Principales responsabilités

Planification stratégique et transformation
- Traduire les priorités de l’entreprise en plans stratégiques, feuilles de route de transformation et cadres d’exécution destinés à être examinés et approuvés par les dirigeants.

- Identifier et évaluer les occasions favorisant la croissance, l’excellence opérationnelle, la valeur client et la résilience de la chaîne d’approvisionnement.

- Utiliser des approches structurées de résolution de problèmes et une analyse fondée sur les données pour relever des défis d’affaires complexes.

- Développer des recommandations stratégiques fondées sur des données probantes ainsi que des modèles opérationnels futurs alignés sur les objectifs d’affaires afin d’éclairer les décisions de la direction.

Élaboration de dossiers d’affaires et réalisation de la valeur
- Diriger et coordonner l’élaboration de dossiers d’affaires, incluant les analyses financières, les évaluations du retour sur investissement (ROI), la modélisation de scénarios et les plans de réalisation des bénéfices.

- Collaborer avec les équipes interfonctionelles afin de valider les opportunités, d’évaluer les pistes de solution et d’éclairer les recommandations et décisions d’investissement.

- Définir les indicateurs de succès et assurer le suivi des résultats afin de confirmer la création de valeur attendue.

- Surveiller et communiquer les progrès, risques, dépendances et écarts afin de soutenir les mesures correctives et la réalisation des bénéfices.

Conseil stratégique et communication exécutive
- Élaborer des présentations exécutives, analyses de rentabilisation, documents d’information et recommandations destinés aux forums de gouvernance et de direction.

- Synthétiser des informations complexes en analyses claires, concises et exploitables pour soutenir la prise de décision.

- Fournir des analyses et recommandations stratégiques afin de faire progresser les priorités clés de l’organisation.

Intégration d’affaires et alignement des parties prenantes
- Animer des ateliers et des séances de planification afin de favoriser l’alignement, de développer des recommandations de priorisation et de faire avancer les discussions stratégiques.

- Collaborer avec les équipes des Opérations, Chaîne d'approvisionnement, Technologie, Finance, Commercial, Livraison de projets et Analyse de données.

- Traduire les objectifs stratégiques en plans de travail exploitables, en jalons et en résultats mesurables.

Innovation de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et mobilisation du changement
- Demeurer au fait des tendances de l’industrie, des produits et technologies émergentes et des changements réglementaires ayant un impact sur la distribution pharmaceutique.

- Évaluer les opportunités innovantes et développer des recommandations visant à améliorer la performance du réseau, l’efficacité opérationnelle, l’expérience client et les capacités de la chaîne d’approvisionnement.

- Soutenir la préparation organisationnelle, l’adoption et l’amélioration continue dans le cadre d’initiatives stratégiques et de programmes de transformation.

Qualifications et expérience

Formation
- Baccalauréat en administration des affaires, commerce, économie, ingénierie, gestion de la chaîne d’approvisionnement ou dans un domaine connexe.

- MBA, maîtrise, certification PMP, Lean Six Sigma ou désignation équivalente considérés comme des atouts.

Expérience
- Minimum de 7 années d’expérience en stratégie, consultation en gestion, transformation d’entreprise, planification corporative, chaîne d’approvisionnement, gestion de projets ou opérations d’affaires.

- Expérience démontrée dans la direction d’initiatives interfonctionnelles ainsi que dans l’élaboration d’analyses de rentabilisation et de recommandations stratégiques.

- Une expérience dans les secteurs de la santé, de la distribution pharmaceutique, de la logistique, du commerce de détail, de la fabrication ou d’autres environnements opérationnels complexes est privilégiée.

Connaissances, compétences et aptitudes

Réflexion stratégique et analytique
- Solide sens des affaires et capacité à relier la stratégie à l’exécution.

- Bon jugement dans l’élaboration de recommandations, l’escalade des risques, la navigation dans l’ambiguïté et l’influence des parties prenantes sans autorité hiérarchique directe.

- Capacité démontrée à résoudre des problèmes complexes grâce à une analyse rigoureuse des données et une approche structurée.

- Solide compréhension financière, incluant les analyses de ROI, l’élaboration de dossiers d’affaires et la réalisation de la valeur.

Communication et influence
- Excellentes aptitudes en présentation, communication et animation.

- Capacité à influencer les parties prenantes et à créer un consensus entre diverses fonctions sans autorité directe.

- Excellentes habiletés en communication exécutive et en développement de relations.

Exécution et leadership
- Capacité à gérer plusieurs priorités dans un environnement dynamique et en constante évolution.

- Capacité à maintenir l’élan des initiatives en coordonnant les intervenants, en mettant en évidence les dépendances et en soutenant les responsables dans l’avancement des actions convenues.

- Sens démontré de l’imputabilité et de la responsabilité quant à la qualité, à la rigueur, au respect des échéanciers et à l’impact des livrables stratégiques sous sa responsabilité.

Maîtrise technologique et numérique
- Maîtrise avancée des applications Microsoft 365, notamment PowerPoint, Excel, Word et Teams.

- Capacité d’utiliser Microsoft Copilot, des outils d’intelligence artificielle et d’autres technologies numériques afin d’améliorer la productivité et la génération d’informations stratégiques.

- Une expérience avec Power BI ou d’autres outils d’analyse et de visualisation de données constitue un atout.

Qualifications supplémentaires

- Le bilinguisme (français et anglais) constitue un atout important.

- Des déplacements occasionnels au Canada peuvent être requis.

*******************************

Position Summary
The Senior Specialist, Business Strategy is a high-impact senior strategic contributor responsible for translating enterprise priorities into actionable business strategies, transformation roadmaps, and value-driven initiatives across McKesson Canada's Pharmaceutical Distribution network.

Working closely with senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders, this role combines strategic thinking, analytical rigor, business case development, and change leadership to solve complex business challenges and enable sustainable growth. The successful candidate will help inform and shape strategic direction by identifying opportunities, developing evidence-based recommendations, and enabling informed decision-making.

Reporting into the Director of Business Strategy & Enablement, this role brings clarity to complex business challenges, aligns stakeholders around a common vision, and influences and enables the achievement of measurable business outcomes that support the long-term evolution of McKesson Canada's supply chain capabilities.

Key Responsibilities
Strategic Planning & Transformation
- Translate enterprise priorities into strategic plans, transformation roadmaps, and execution frameworks for review and endorsement by senior business leaders.

- Identify and evaluate opportunities that drive growth, operational excellence, customer value, and supply chain resilience.

- Apply structured problem-solving and data-driven analysis to address complex business challenges.

- Develop evidence-based strategic recommendations and future-state operating models aligned with business objectives to inform leadership decisions.

Business Case Development & Value Realization
- Lead and coordinate the development of business cases, including financial analysis, ROI assessments, scenario modelling, and benefit realization plans.

- Partner with cross-functional teams to validate opportunities, evaluate opportunities, and inform investment recommendations and decisions.

- Define success measures and track outcomes to ensure initiatives deliver intended value.

- Monitor and report progress, risks, dependencies, and variances to support corrective action and benefit realization.

Executive Advisory & Strategic Communications
- Develop executive presentations, business cases, briefing materials, and recommendations for leadership and governance forums.

- Synthesize complex information into clear, concise insights that support decision-making.

- Provide strategic analysis and recommendations to advance key business priorities.

Business Integration & Stakeholder Alignment
- Facilitate workshops and planning sessions to build alignment, develop prioritization recommendations, and advance strategic discussions.

- Collaborate across Operations, Supply Chain, Technology, Finance, Commercial, Project Delivery and Data Analytics teams.

- Translate strategic objectives into actionable workstreams, milestones, and measurable outcomes.

Supply Chain Innovation & Change Enablement
- Monitor industry trends, emerging technologies and products, and regulatory developments impacting pharmaceutical distribution.

- Evaluate innovative opportunities and develop recommendations intended to enhance network performance, operational efficiency, customer experience, and supply chain capabilities.

- Support organizational readiness, adoption, and continuous improvement efforts for strategic initiatives and transformative programs.

Qualifications & Experience
Education
- Bachelor’s degree in business administration, Commerce, Economics, Engineering, Supply Chain Management, or a related field.

- MBA, Master's degree, PMP, Lean Six Sigma, or equivalent designation is considered an asset.

Experience

The Senior Program Manager, Oncology and Multispecialty Strategy   Tech Strategy   leads the execution and continuous improvement of New Solutions Enablement across The US Oncology Network. The role manages multiple related initiatives within a complex program, coordinating intake, technology, cybersecurity, data governance, procurement, vendor management, legal, and IT service management reviews to ensure requests align with business priorities, McKesson standards, and expected outcomes.

Working with the Governance Lead, Sr. Product Program Manager, requesting practices, business leaders, and technology partners, this role defines and refines scope, facilitates cross-team planning, manages interdependencies, resolves resource and workflow gaps, and maintains clear accountability for milestones, decisions, and next actions. The Senior Program Manager provides indirect leadership across participating teams and   operates   with autonomy in a matrixed environment.

The successful candidate combines program management discipline, business and technical awareness, strong stakeholder influence, and data-driven decision-making. This role turns a complex, multi-system process into a transparent and trusted program while ensuring that speed does not compromise cybersecurity, data, vendor, legal, technology, or service management requirements.

Key Responsibilities

Program Planning and Strategic Alignment

- Lead scope definition and refinement with business, practice, and technical stakeholders, ensuring New Solutions Enablement activities align with business goals, technology strategy, and approved governance requirements.

- Develop and   maintain   an integrated program plan, milestones, decision points, resource needs, and dependencies across multiple concurrent solution requests and review workstreams.

- Facilitate complex cross-initiative planning discussions,   identify   prerequisites, and coordinate solutions to resource or scheduling gaps across participating teams.

- Define program success criteria with sponsors and stakeholders, connecting operational targets to transparency, compliance, cycle time, stakeholder experience, and business value.

Program Execution and Cross-Functional Delivery

- Lead day-to-day execution across intake, assessment, review, approval, cataloging, and closure, ensuring each request has a clear owner,   current status , next action, and target milestone.

- Manage complex dependencies and handoffs across Cybersecurity, Data Governance, Procurement, Vendor Management, Legal, IT Service Management, architecture, technology teams, and requesting practices.

- Lead scope and priority trade-off discussions, drive agreement on changes, and ensure decisions are documented, approved, and communicated across affected stakeholders.

- Provide indirect leadership to cross-functional contributors, remove roadblocks, resolve conflicts, and escalate high-impact issues with recommended actions.

Governance, Risk, and Compliance

- Ensure each request is evaluated against applicable McKesson technology, cybersecurity, data governance, vendor due diligence, legal, architecture, and IT service management standards before advancement.

- Independently   identify , assess, prioritize, and manage risks and issues across multiple requests;   maintain   risk and issue records, execute mitigation plans, and communicate significant exposures to program leadership.

- Establish clear escalation paths and ensure exceptions are surfaced for decision rather than bypassed or resolved outside approved governance processes.

- Maintain complete,   accurate , and audit-ready program records across Asana and related systems of record, including status, ownership, decisions, conditions, approvals, and supporting documentation.

Stakeholder Management and Communication

- Establish a strong cross-functional stakeholder network and serve as a trusted point of coordination for practices, business leaders, review teams, vendors, and technology partners.

- Maintain feedback loops with key stakeholders to   identify   program adjustments that improve business value, predictability, and requester experience.

- Develop and execute a stakeholder communication plan that provides clear status, risks, decisions, impacts, and next steps for different audiences.

- Partner with senior stakeholders to resolve conflicts, negotiate commitments, manage expectations, and sustain alignment without direct authority.

Performance Reporting and Business Value

- Develop and   maintain   dashboards, scorecards, and executive reporting for request volume, aging, cycle time, SLA performance, risk, dependencies, bottlenecks, and decision status.

- Support adoption of new ways of working by aligning stakeholders on the   program   vision, benefits, roles, and expected behaviors.

- Demonstrated experience managing multiple medium-to-large initiatives within a complex project or program where delivery outcomes carry meaningful business, operational, regulatory, or technology impact.

- Proven ability to manage integrated plans, milestones, scope, dependencies, risks, issues, resources, governance activities, and executive reporting with substantial autonomy.

- Experience leading cross-functional work and influencing business and technology stakeholders without direct authority.

- Experience applying enterprise delivery methodologies, governance standards, workflow tools, and performance reporting practices in a matrixed organization.

- Healthcare, health technology,   regulated-industry , technology governance, vendor intake, risk management, cybersecurity, data governance, procurement, or legal review experience is preferred.

Required Skills and Competencies

- Risk and dependency   management:   independently   identifies   complex and interrelated risks,   develops   mitigation actions,   manages   cross-team dependencies, and proactively escalates significant issues with recommendations.

- Stakeholder management and   influence:   builds long-term working relationships, adapts communication to the audience, resolves conflict, and drives consensus and accountability across functional groups.

- Judgment and discretion: handles vendor, contracting, regulated, and confidential information appropriately and applies standards consistently in an evolving environment.

Measures of Success

This role offers location flexibility and is open to candidates across the United States.

Candidates based in the Dallas–Fort Worth (DFW) area will be hired in a hybrid capacity and are expected to work onsite at our Las Colinas office a minimum of two (2) days per week, with the remaining days worked remotely. Specific in‑office days may be designated based on team needs and business priorities.

About the Role:

The Director, Strategy – U.S. Pharmaceutical Distribution serves as a trusted individual contributor within the North America Pharmaceutical Distribution Strategy function. U.S. Pharmaceutical Distribution, or USPD, is the backbone of McKesson’s pharmaceutical operations, with over 9,000 employees and a mission to ensure our customers and patients get what they need, when they need it. Reporting to the VP, Segment Strategy, this position operates as a key strategic partner to segment leadership in a targeted USPD business segment: Strategic, Community & Specialized Pharmacy (SCS), McKesson Health Systems (MHS), Commercial Strategy & Innovation (CSI), or Supply Chain Operations (SCO).

The Director is responsible for leading and supporting defined workstreams and strategic sub-areas within the segment, shaping insights, framing decisions, and driving forward progress in close partnership with business and functional leaders. This role requires sound strategic and financial analysis, strong communication and stakeholder engagement, and a commitment to developing strategy collaboratively—not in isolation.

Success in this role is defined by the ability to translate complex dynamics into actionable decisions, build credibility with partners, and ensure strategic work leads to practical, executable outcomes.

What You'll Do:

Strategic Analysis & Insight
- Own end-to-end analytical workstreams within larger strategic initiatives — from problem structuring and hypothesis development through analysis and synthesis of findings — with guidance from initiative leads on framing and prioritization.

- Build rigorous fact bases on market structure, competitor strategies and economics, customer segments, and channel dynamics across the pharmaceutical distribution value chain.

- Synthesize complex quantitative and qualitative information into clear, well-structured storylines; consistently deliver the “so what,” not just the analysis.

- Identify implications of your own workstream for the overall initiative, and flag issues and opportunities to initiative leadership proactively.

Value Chain & Financial Analysis
- Build and maintain financial models that translate market shifts — reimbursement changes, sourcing dynamics, customer mix evolution, competitive moves — into quantified P&L implications for the business, with review from senior team members.

- Develop working knowledge of how each participant in the pharmaceutical value chain — manufacturers, distributors, PBMs, payers, and pharmacies — earns, protects, and seeks to expand its economic position.

- Track and analyze legislative, regulatory, and policy developments — including drug pricing reform, PBM transparency requirements, and reimbursement policy changes — and support the assessment of their financial and competitive implications.

- Support scenario and sensitivity analysis: pressure-test the assumptions that matter most and help bound the range of plausible outcomes.

Problem Solving & Collaboration
- Participate actively in team problem solving; step up to lead portions of problem-solving sessions with the team and with business partners.

- Challenge assumptions constructively and take intellectual risks to generate new ideas; bring curiosity about how the distribution business actually works economically.

- Manage your own time and workplan effectively; know how and when to seek input; control the quality of your own work product.

Communication & Stakeholder Support
- Prepare well-written, logical, concise documents and executive materials with minimal guidance; lead with key messages.

- Present analysis and recommendations with confidence to initiative teams and, with preparation, to senior business audiences.

- Build collaborative working relationships with business, finance, sourcing, commercial, and functional partners; project credibility and reliability.

Team & Function Contribution
- Coach analysts and newer team members on analytical craft, modeling standards, and story-lining; provide constructive upward feedback.

- Contribute to strategy function-building efforts — recruiting, knowledge capture, analytical tooling, and ways of working.

Basic Requirements:
- 7+ years of progressive experience in strategy consulting, corporate strategy, investment banking, private equity, or comparable analytically intensive roles.

- Exposure to healthcare, pharmaceutical services, or distribution businesses strongly preferred; genuine interest in the economics of the pharmaceutical value chain is essential.

- Demonstrated advanced financial modeling capability — building models from a blank sheet that connect market dynamics to P&L outcomes.

- Track record of structuring ambiguous problems, executing rigorous analysis, and producing executive-ready synthesis and deliverables.

- Experience working effectively in cross-functional teams and managing multiple deliverables under time pressure.

Preferred Skills/Experience:
- Structured Problem Solver:  Formulates clear hypotheses and structures workstreams well with light guidance; handles complex analyses with little oversight and moves efficiently from data to insight.

- Financial Modeling & P&L Literacy:  Builds financial models as strategic tools — not to forecast with false precision but to identify the assumptions that matter and quantify the implications of strategic choices.

- Synthesis & Storylining:  Distills complex information into clear, logical storylines; writes and charts at near executive-ready quality; consistently answers “so what.”

- Value Chain Curiosity:  Demonstrates genuine intellectual curiosity about how distribution, sourcing, pharmacy, PBM, and payer economics actually work — and is building working fluency in them.

- Collaborative Teammate:  Is a reliable, helpful, and proactive teammate; builds trust with partners across the business; coaches junior colleagues and is open to coaching from others.

- Communication:  Writes clearly and concisely; presents with confidence in familiar settings; listens well and tailors style and tone to the audience.

- Must have the ability to travel up to 20% of the time
- Candidates that reside within 50 miles of Irving, TX will be required to be onsite 2 days per week.

You will manage all aspects of the program from pre-planning through implementation, cutover, and post-go-live stabilization; plan and facilitate the work to deliver on time, in budget, and within scope; manage program-level risks, dependencies, budget, and escalated issues; and keep business and technology partners engaged and aligned throughout. The modernization is just the beginning. This is a standing leadership role for McKesson’s B2B Specialty eCommerce space, not a fixed term assignment: once the new platform is live, you will continue as its delivery leader, driving the execution of the platform’s forward roadmap and leading the enhancements, new capabilities, and strategic initiatives that build on the foundation you put in place. This is a chance to help transform how McKesson’s Oncology & Multispecialty business serves its customers — and to keep shaping that transformation well beyond launch.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Program leadership
Serve as the Program Manager accountable for leading McKesson’s B2B Specialty eCommerce application through a full platform modernization, managing all aspects from pre-planning through implementation, cutover, and post-go-live stabilization. Operate with significant autonomy as the senior point of accountability for the program’s delivery, driving complex, high-stakes decisions to resolution in close partnership with leadership. Oversee and manage this large, complex, critical program in partnership with leadership, keeping it aligned to strategic business goals and objectives and regularly assessing whether the outcomes are being met. Lead the teams and partners involved in the program through influence, setting the standard for how the work is delivered and mentoring others on best practices and methodologies. Carry that accountability forward beyond the modernization, leading the ongoing portfolio of enhancements, new capabilities, and strategic initiatives for the B2B Specialty eCommerce space as the platform’s long-term delivery leader. Turn the platform’s multi-year roadmap into executable plans — sequencing the work, securing the resources, and holding delivery to commitments — and bring the delivery insight, feasibility read, and trade-off analysis that shape what makes the roadmap and in what order.

Planning & business alignment
Break program objectives down into measurable business outcomes and ensure alignment with business and IT goals and strategy. Partner with program sponsors to gain their support and build the program roadmap, turning goals into concrete plans with timelines and deliverables. Coordinate across all groups involved — business, delivery, technical teams, operations, and change management — to define and manage program scope, and establish appropriate governance in line with organizational policies.

Budget management
Use advanced tools and techniques to estimate program costs; develop and control the program budget and manage expenditure within agreed spending plans. Continuously monitor actual cost versus budget, evaluate factors that may drive cost changes, and partner with finance and delivery stakeholders to keep budget decisions tied to program priorities and expected results.

Stakeholder management & collaboration
Act as a trusted advisor to executive sponsors and senior leaders, building strong relationships across the business, technology, and partner teams involved in the program. Lead the program’s steering and review cadence — giving executives clear, honest status, surfacing key decisions and trade-offs, and negotiating priorities and program needs.

Execution
Facilitate program scope trade-off conversations with a broad range of stakeholders, influencing strategic decisions. Identify and manage dependencies within the program, resolving conflicts and optimizing resources; remove roadblocks by working through conflicts and resolving issues. Coordinate and manage the strategic implementation partner delivering the packaged commercial software, holding the vendor accountable for scope, schedule, budget, and quality, and ensuring their work integrates cleanly with McKesson teams and program objectives. Maintain oversight of the entire program lifecycle, collaborating with IT leaders and stakeholders across all SDLC phases, and balance the availability of required skills and competencies across the program. Drive launch readiness, cutover, and go-live, then lead the post-go-live stabilization period to ensure a smooth, low-disruption transition to the new platform.

Performance & results
Work with business sponsors to track the results the program delivers, confirm the expected benefits are achieved, and find opportunities to deliver more. Maintain the program dashboard and documentation; serve as the first-level escalation path for performance issues; evaluate and optimize overall program performance; facilitate lessons-learned and retrospective sessions and implement the results. Use AI-enabled delivery tools to track progress, anticipate risks, and support faster, better-informed decisions.

Risk management
Identify and manage risk at the program level, consolidating risks across the program’s workstreams; develop and govern program level risk plans, processes, and systems. Oversee creation and execution of action plans for program risks, maintain and review the program issues list, and proactively escalate risks to senior leadership.

Change & continuous improvement
Lead change management across the program: align sponsors and stakeholders on the vision and benefits, and help teams adopt the new platform and ways of working. Drive continuous improvement by applying proven delivery practices and standards, capturing lessons learned, and using program data and reporting to strengthen how the program runs over time.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING
- 10+ years of program management experience, including several years leading large-scale enterprise technology deployments from strategy through delivery.

- Hands-on experience delivering SAP programs.

- Exceptional written and verbal communication, including a proven ability to brief, influence, and build confidence with executive audiences.

- Proven experience coordinating and managing a systems integrator or implementation partner through a packaged commercial software delivery, holding the vendor accountable to SOW, scope, schedule, budget, and quality commitments.

- Strong command of program management methodologies (Agile and traditional), enterprise delivery tools and frameworks, and delivery governance.

- Hands-on experience running planning, tracking, resource management, and vendor administration through enterprise program and portfolio management tooling — Planview, Smartsheet, Jira, Microsoft Project, and SAP Fieldglass are the platforms in use here. Experience with all of them is not expected; a demonstrated track record with tools of this kind is.

- Comfort using AI-enabled and data-driven delivery tools for planning, tracking, reporting, and risk forecasting.

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

- Ability to travel up to 25% of the time.

- You are calm under pressure, resilient through setbacks, and a sharp problem-solver with strong business judgment — someone who brings order, focus, and confidence to a complex, high-stakes program.

Preferred Skills/Experience
- SAP Commerce Cloud experience; eCommerce modernization experience, particularly in B2B and/or health care commerce; background in pharmaceutical distribution or another regulated industry

- Master’s degree in Business Administration, Computer Science, Information Technology or a related field;

- PMP, PgMP, PMI-ACP, SAFe, Lean Portfolio Management, Agile/Scrum, or equivalent certifications.

Position Summary
The Transformation Manager – Integrated Program Office will serve as a strategic leader responsible for driving company-wide change initiatives that enhance operational efficiency, enable innovation, and support long-term business objectives. This role will oversee the transformation portfolio, optimize program management processes and tools, and deliver executive-level reporting to inform decision-making and governance.

·       Portfolio Governance & Optimization: Establish and refine portfolio management processes to improve initiative prioritization, resource allocation, and performance tracking across the transformation landscape.
·       Program Management: Provide guidance, leadership and transformation support for execution and shorten time to value through waterfall and agile methodologies.
·       Tool Strategy & Enablement: Evaluate, implement, and optimize program and portfolio management and execution tools to support scalable execution, data integrity, and user adoption across business units.

·       Continuous Improvement & Innovation: Champion a culture of continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to streamline processes, enhance capabilities, and accelerate transformation outcomes.
·       Organizational Support: Provide financial management for the Office of the CIO and manage licensing and vendors for Portfolio and Program Management tools and resources.
·       Successful people leader: Demonstrated ability to build, maintain and recruit high performing teams through trust, inclusion, and psychological safety. Coach and develops talent, communicate with empathy, and balances employee well-being with accountability and results.

About McKesson Medical-Surgical
McKesson Medical-Surgical (MMS), which is expected to become Wellverse in early 2027, is a subsidiary and publicly reported segment of the McKesson Corporation. MMS distributes medical-surgical supplies, pharmaceuticals, diagnostic equipment and supplies, along with other solutions and services to virtually every type of healthcare setting and provider outside of the traditional hospital. These markets – often referred to as Alternate Care or Non-Acute Care – include physician offices, surgery centers, long-term care providers, laboratories, home health and hospice agencies, health systems, government facilities and online marketplaces and retailers.

jobs.title: Directeur(trice) principal(e), Finance - Planification et Analyse Financières d'entreprise / Senior Director, Finance - Corporate FP&A
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

Résumé du poste
Le Directeur principal, Finance – FP&A corporatif, est responsable de l’élaboration, de la communication et de la mise en œuvre de la planification et de l’analyse financières pour la consolidation de McKesson Canada. Il agit comme principal interlocuteur financier auprès de McKesson Corporate et des équipes de direction des différentes unités d’affaires pour les prévisions, le budget, le plan à long terme ainsi que pour tout projet ponctuel nécessitant une analyse financière. Il conseille la haute direction en tant que partenaire d’affaires dans la consolidation des budgets, des prévisions et des plans à long terme, tant au niveau stratégique que tactique.

Responsabilités principales
• Agir comme partenaire d’affaires et conseiller financier clé auprès du VP, Finance, FP&A corporatif, ainsi que du CFO.
• Diriger et superviser toutes les activités liées à la planification et à l’analyse financières pour l’unité d’affaires de McKesson Canada, incluant notamment les rapports financiers, les budgets annuels, les prévisions mensuelles, les revues opérationnelles trimestrielles, les plans à long terme et les analyses financières ponctuelles.
• Conseiller la haute direction sur les implications financières des décisions d’affaires, identifier et gérer les risques et opportunités associés aux opérations et au plan à long terme (consolidation McKesson Canada).
• Fournir du soutien stratégique, de la planification de scénarios, ainsi que des analyses de risques et d’opportunités afin d’atteindre les objectifs financiers prévus et à long terme.
• Diriger le développement d’évaluations continues des objectifs financiers stratégiques à court et long terme et recommander des solutions aux parties prenantes, en tenant compte des facteurs internes et externes, de l’impact du marché, de la législation et de l’alignement avec les objectifs financiers corporatifs.
• Diriger les discussions et favoriser le consensus entre les équipes sur les sujets interdépendants entre les BU.
• Jouer un rôle clé dans l’avancement de la stratégie FP&A de McKesson Canada à travers les différents groupes.
• Soutenir l’équipe dans l’identification et la mise en œuvre de stratégies visant à maximiser la précision des prévisions au sein des différentes unités d’affaires.
• Appuyer l’équipe dans les livrables de fin de mois.
• S’assurer qu’à un niveau consolidé, les objectifs budgétaires sont atteints et que la croissance attendue pour les années futures est adéquate. Communiquer clairement au VP, Finance FP&A et M&A ainsi qu’aux CFO des BU les risques et opportunités pour l’année en cours et les années futures.
• Diriger des équipes interfonctionnelles pour suivre la performance des indicateurs clés par rapport au budget ou aux analyses financières prévues.
• Déterminer les normes et indicateurs permettant de mesurer la performance financière de McKesson Canada.
• Concevoir et communiquer des modèles flexibles (tests de résistance, gestion des dépenses, analyse coûts variables vs coûts fixes, etc.) afin d’assurer une communication efficace avec les parties prenantes et une intégration fluide dans les processus de clôture mensuelle, de prévision et de budgétisation annuelle.
• Identifier et communiquer les KPI/indicateurs clés à la haute direction, en mettant en lumière leur impact global sur l’entreprise avec des rapports clairs et concis.
• Assurer un environnement de contrôle interne hautement efficace et veiller au respect de tous les processus SOX dans le cadre du budget et du plan à long terme.

Analyse et performance financière
• Diriger l’analyse des résultats financiers de l’entreprise en lien avec les profits, tendances, coûts, et conformité aux budgets, prévisions et plan à long terme.
• Surveiller les résultats financiers mensuels, trimestriels et annuels et recommander des solutions stratégiques essentielles à la croissance de l’entreprise.
• Développer et mettre en œuvre des KPI appropriés et ponctuels pour l’équipe de direction des BU, ainsi que des indicateurs permettant la gestion en temps réel des activités.
• Remettre en question les soumissions financières des BU pour les budgets, plans à long terme et prévisions continues afin d’assurer que les économies nécessaires sont prises en compte et que les coûts sont correctement reflétés.
• Guider la direction dans le développement des hypothèses mensuelles lors des prévisions et du rolling forecast ; élaborer des plans de réussite pour les budgets et le plan à long terme qui seront examinés et approuvés par l’équipe de direction exécutive.
• Agir comme partenaire d’affaires du groupe des relations avec les investisseurs chez Corporate pour représenter les principaux moteurs et la performance du Canada par rapport à l’année précédente.
• Diriger et soutenir les initiatives d’amélioration des processus et les projets de mise en œuvre de systèmes liés à la planification financière (incluant les projets dirigés par le corporate).

Responsabilités générales
• Agir comme la ressource principale de l’entreprise dans son domaine d’expertise, en fournissant leadership et orientation sur tous les enjeux connexes.
• Promouvoir les principes I2CARE et ILEAD de McKesson Canada et de McKesson, en démontrant l’exemple et en encourageant les autres à faire de même.
• Gérer efficacement l’équipe : soutenir, guider et diriger le personnel. Favoriser un haut niveau d’engagement, déléguer adéquatement et fournir orientation, soutien et attentes claires.
• Encourager une communication ouverte, constructive et en temps opportun. Effectuer l’évaluation des performances des employés et soutenir leur développement.
• Promouvoir la collaboration au sein de l’équipe et entre les différents groupes et départements.
• Maintenir une communication appropriée avec tous les niveaux de l’organisation.
• Veiller au respect des politiques de l’entreprise.

Qualifications
• Baccalauréat en commerce avec spécialisation en finance ou comptabilité. Titre comptable professionnel (CPA) requis ; solide expertise comptable.
• Minimum de 15 années d’expérience en comptabilité et gestion dans un rôle similaire, incluant au moins 10 années d’expérience en FP&A, idéalement dans une entreprise internationale.
• Expérience démontrée en interaction avec la haute direction et en développement de stratégies financières innovantes.
• Maîtrise approfondie de la planification et de l’analyse financières, des systèmes associés, ainsi que des principes économiques et analytiques liés aux affaires.
• Pensée stratégique, innovante et proactive, avec désir de travailler dans un environnement en évolution.
• Présence exécutive : capacité à interagir avec les dirigeants, influencer sans autorité et défendre ses positions.
• Habileté démontrée à gérer plusieurs livrables simultanément avec un fort sens de l’urgence.
• Excellente communication et fortes capacités d’influence.
• Esprit d’équipe, leadership et excellentes aptitudes interpersonnelles.
• Esprit analytique et stratégique, sens de l’organisation, autonomie.
• Capacité à synthétiser des analyses complexes en recommandations claires pour la haute direction.
• Leader de talent capable de maintenir une culture d’excellence.
• Jugement exceptionnel, initiative, rapidité d’apprentissage.
• Bilinguisme (oral et écrit).
• Connaissance avancée des systèmes financiers (ERP, suite Microsoft Office, etc.) ; la connaissance de SAP, HFM et BPC constitue un atout.

The Principal M&A Analyst Enterprise Applications is responsible for the assessment, planning and execution of enterprise application initiatives supporting technology due diligence, integration planning, and integration cost estimation activities for mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, and strategic business initiatives.
Reporting to the VP, MT M&A this role serves as the primary Enterprise Applications representative within M&A transactions and partners closely with Enterprise Applications Service Area leaders, Enterprise Architecture, Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, and Business Unit IT teams, and acts as a trusted advisor to Corporate Development stakeholders to evaluate application landscapes, identify integration requirements and strategy, assess risks, and develop cost estimates.
The role requires broad knowledge of enterprise application architectures, business process alignment, data migration considerations, integration patterns, and large-scale SaaS implementation and transformation programs.
The successful candidate will be comfortable operating in highly dynamic and ambiguous environments, translating incomplete information into practical recommendations and estimates that support executive decision-making and deal value realization. The role requires a high degree of discretion, as it will be privy to non-public information that must not be disclosed to tower leaders, while still engaging them for high-level input to inform planning.

What You'll Do
M&A Due Diligence & Application Assessment
- Lead enterprise application due diligence activities for acquisitions, divestitures, and strategic transactions.
- Assess target application portfolios, architecture, integrations, business process alignment, and technology dependencies.
- Evaluate application complexity, technical debt, support models, licensing considerations, vendor dependencies, and integration risks.
- Identify application rationalization, consolidation, modernization, and synergy opportunities.
- Document findings and recommendations for inclusion in due diligence reports and executive readouts.

Integration Strategy & Planning
- Develop high level application integration and migration strategies aligned to business objectives and enterprise standards.

- Support development of Day 1, Employee Day 1, and Initial Integration plans.
- Facilitate discovery and planning workshops with business stakeholders, application owners, architects, and service area SMEs.
- Develop transition roadmaps, implementation sequencing, and dependency management plans.

Cost Modeling & Financial Analysis
- Develop application integration cost estimates and financial models to support transaction evaluations and integration planning.
- Build cost estimates for: - Microsoft 365 tenant migrations
- Workday implementations and tenant consolidation
- SAP ECC and SAP S/4HANA migrations
- CRM transitions
- Data migration and application decommissioning activities
- Integration platform and middleware implementations

- Collaborate with service area SMEs, vendors, and implementation partners to develop realistic estimates, assumptions, timelines, and resource requirements.
- Document risks, dependencies, confidence levels, and alternative implementation scenarios.

Enterprise Applications Domain Leadership
- Provide expertise across enterprise application architectures and integration patterns.
- Demonstrate broad understanding of: - ERP platforms (SAP ECC and SAP S/4HANA)
- Productivity and Collaboration platforms (Microsoft 365)
- HCM and HRIS systems (Workday)
- ITSM platforms (ServiceNow)
- CRM platforms (Salesforce)
- Contact Center solutions (Five 9s)
- Middleware and integration technologies
- Identity and access integrations
- Data migration and master data management concepts

- Assess application interoperability, data dependencies, and impacts to business operations.
- Partner with Enterprise Architecture to align integration strategies with technology standards and future-state roadmaps.

Cross-Functional Collaboration
- Identify and engage the appropriate application teams, architects, business analysts, product owners, and SMEs required for each transaction.
- Coordinate activities across Enterprise Applications, Infrastructure, Cloud, Cybersecurity, Data & AI, Enterprise Architecture, and Business Unit organizations.
- Facilitate decision-making and alignment on integration assumptions, migration strategies, timelines, and resource requirements.
- Build strong relationships across matrixed teams to drive successful transaction outcomes.

Delivery Excellence
- Manage multiple concurrent diligence while balancing competing priorities and aggressive timelines.
- Ensure quality, consistency, and completeness of application-related deliverables.
- Contribute to the continuous improvement of M&A delivery methodologies, application assessment frameworks, integration planning templates, and estimation models.
- Continuously improve playbooks and processes for Due Diligence, identifying and incorporating lessons learned and best practices to improve future transaction outcomes.

Basic Requirements
- 13+ years of professional experience, including 8+ years in Enterprise Applications, ERP platforms, Solution Architecture, Digital Transformation, or IT Program Delivery.
- Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, Finance, Engineering, or a related field.
- Experience conducting technology due diligence and technology risk assessments for mergers and acquisitions.
- Experience presenting complex technology recommendations, cost models and business impacts to senior executives.
- Demonstrated success leading large-scale, cross-functional initiatives in complex enterprise environments.

Preferred Skills/Experience
- MBA or other advanced degree.
- Experience in healthcare, pharmaceutical, distribution, supply chain, or other highly regulated industries.
- Experience evaluating cloud environments, data platforms, cybersecurity controls, and digital transformation initiatives during M&A transactions.
- Knowledge of financial modeling, synergy planning, valuation support, and business case development.
- Expertise in portfolio optimization, demand management, and strategic investment planning.
- Experience with enterprise portfolio management tools and data-driven decision-making frameworks.
- Strong change management and organizational transformation experience.
- Experience leading global or multi-business-unit integrations.
- Broad understanding of: - Enterprise application architecture principles

- Identity and access integrations

McKesson is seeking a Principal M&A Analyst Cyber to support cybersecurity due diligence and risk assessment activities across mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, and strategic investments. This role serves as a trusted advisor to business and technology stakeholders, helping evaluate target-company cybersecurity programs, identify risks, document findings, and support integration planning.
The successful candidate will partner with cybersecurity, legal, compliance, technology, and business teams to assess security posture, recommend remediation strategies, and help protect enterprise value throughout the transaction lifecycle. This role is ideal for a cybersecurity professional who combines strong analytical skills, risk management expertise, and collaborative leadership.

What You'll Do
Enterprise Cybersecurity Due Diligence Leadership
- Lead cybersecurity due diligence assessments for mergers, acquisitions, and strategic transactions.
- Evaluate target company security controls, governance practices, regulatory compliance, and cyber risks.
- Document cybersecurity findings, risk ratings, and remediation requirements for stakeholders and executive audiences.
- Coordinate with security, infrastructure, application, privacy, and compliance teams on integration risk assessments.
- Assess third-party, cloud, identity, vulnerability, and data protection risks associated with acquisition targets.
- Provide actionable recommendations that help inform transaction decisions and post-close integration planning.
- Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders to ensure cybersecurity risks are tracked, mitigated, and communicated effectively.

Financial and Integration Planning Inputs
- Own the cybersecurity contribution to the transaction cost model, including preliminary one-time and recurring cost estimates, assumptions, contingencies, and key estimation risks.
