- Partner with Finance, Cybersecurity Service Areas, Infrastructure, Enterprise Applications, Enterprise Architecture, and MT M&A leadership to ensure cybersecurity risk and cost implications are reflected consistently in deal materials.

Strategic Deal Advisory and Executive Influence
- Translate complex cybersecurity findings into clear business implications, including potential deal impact, risk acceptance requirements, cost exposure, timing constraints, and integration complexity.
- Identify, prioritize, and escalate material or potentially deal-altering cybersecurity risks, with practical recommendations and clearly articulated trade-offs.
- Advise transaction leaders on cybersecurity considerations affecting valuation, deal structure, contractual protections, closing conditions, transition services, and investment requirements.
- Deliver concise, decision-oriented cybersecurity recommendations to executive leadership.
- Serve as the senior cybersecurity diligence advisor in high-ambiguity situations where evidence is incomplete, timelines are compressed, and decisions carry significant enterprise consequence.

Governance, Standards, and Capability Building
- Establish and maintain enterprise standards, playbooks, templates, quality criteria, and escalation thresholds for M&A cybersecurity due diligence.
- Provide portfolio-level visibility into cybersecurity diligence status, material risk themes, cost exposure, and recurring integration complexity across concurrent transactions.

- Significant experience leading cybersecurity due diligence or cyber risk assessment for mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, strategic investments, or similarly complex enterprise transactions.
- Knowledge of NIST CSF, ISO 27001, HITRUST, SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR, and other relevant security or privacy frameworks.
- Experience evaluating security controls across cloud, infrastructure, applications, identity, and data protection domains.
- Strong stakeholder management and cross-functional collaboration skills.
- Proven written and verbal communication skills with the ability to present risk information clearly.
- Recognized expertise in enterprise cybersecurity risk, control environments, security architecture, regulatory considerations, and integration complexity.
- Demonstrated ability to shape executive decisions through clear risk, financial, and strategic recommendations.
- Experience directing cross-functional work through influence in highly matrixed, time-sensitive, and confidential environments.
- Strong financial acumen, including cost estimation, assumption development, scenario analysis, and communication of uncertainty.

Preferred Skills/Experience
- Experience assessing regulatory and compliance considerations, including privacy and data protection requirements.
- Familiarity with cyber threat management, vulnerability management, incident response, or security operations.
- Experience developing cybersecurity governance processes, assessment methodologies, or due diligence frameworks.
- Professional certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CCSP, GIAC, or relevant cloud security certifications.
- Experience supporting post-acquisition integration planning and risk remediation programs.

The role will focus on business partnerships with members of the overall organization to assist in meeting organizational and financial goals, evolve metrics and reporting to manage the company’s financial health, and oversee all end-to-end financial processes including P&L Consolidations, reporting of financial results, and planning, and analysis. The role ensures that strategies are appropriately reflected in company budgets, forecasts, and long-range planning and most importantly, provide value-added analysis and insights which drive sound decision-making.

Responsibilities:
- Lead the financial planning (budget, forecast, long range plan) process for all functional areas. Assist in providing strategic decision support, scenario planning and identify key drivers, risks, opportunities and plans for potential mitigation.

- Provide actual to budget/forecast reporting, dashboards, and variance analyses to business partners to enable decision making and alignment to achieving company objectives.

- Partner with executive leadership to prepare QBR, Board and other investor related materials and presentations.

- Analyze and present complex financial information in simple terms, presenting conclusions and recommendations to business leaders.

- Provide business support to the other FP&A teams to help create transparency of key assumptions in critical business areas.

- Collaborate and work with accounting group and create a synergized partnership to ensure month-end close and accurate accounting for all areas of the business.

- Support broader organization through ad hoc projects and analysis and provide insightful analytics to highlight risks and opportunities.

- Manage a team of three; Cultivating high performance teams and facilitating career development while leading is a must.

Qualifications:
- Bachelor's Degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field required; MBA preferred.

- 7+ years of successful progressive Finance experience required

- Minimum of 3+ years supervisory experience required

- Willing to challenge common assumptions.

- Eager to pitch in and assist as necessary to help the team accomplish functional and corporate goals.

- Strong sense of drive and initiative.

About McKesson Medical-Surgical
McKesson Medical-Surgical (MMS), which is expected to become Wellverse in early 2027, is a subsidiary and publicly reported segment of the McKesson Corporation. MMS distributes medical-surgical supplies, pharmaceuticals, diagnostic equipment and supplies, along with other solutions and services to virtually every type of healthcare setting and provider outside of the traditional hospital. These markets – often referred to as Alternate Care or Non-Acute Care – include physician offices, surgery centers, long-term care providers, laboratories, home health and hospice agencies, health systems, government facilities and online marketplaces and retailers.

Alternate Care markets are growing rapidly and MMS is proud to be a leader in this space. With a team of approximately 8,000 employees, a network of 15 distribution centers and approximately 900 delivery vehicles, we collaborate with more than 2,200 leading manufacturers and serve over 200,000 customer accounts across the U.S. Our catalog includes more than 270,000 SKUs of branded and private-label medical-surgical products – from bandages to specialty pharmaceuticals and COVID-19 tests.

The Director, Revenue Cycle Management FP&A provides strategic and hands-on financial leadership for The US Oncology Network’s Revenue Cycle Management organization. Reporting to the Senior Director, Revenue Cycle Management Finance, this role defines the RCM FP&A agenda and directly develops and leads the analyses, models, forecasts, reporting, and executive materials required to advance priority work across transformation economics, cash and working capital, revenue and reserve performance, and practice-level financial outcomes.

The Director serves as the senior FP&A partner to Revenue Cycle Operations, Finance, Accounting, practice leadership, and senior executives while remaining actively engaged in execution. The role develops and reviews detailed financial models, performs and guides variance investigation, prepares decision-ready materials, and resolves ambiguous financial questions while setting governance, integrating priorities, and directing cross-functional workstreams. The Director manages the Senior Manager, Revenue Cycle Management FP&A and establishes priorities, review standards, coaching, and scalable ways of working for the function.

Key Responsibilities
Strategic FP&A Leadership and Business Partnership
- Define and direct the RCM financial planning, forecasting, and performance-management strategy, with direct ownership and execution of high-priority or highly complex forecasts, models, analyses, and deliverables.
- Advise RCM Operations and Finance executives on choices, risks, opportunities, tradeoffs, and recommended actions; influence decisions across organizational boundaries.
- Build and maintain an integrated performance framework that connects financial, operational, and practice outcomes and creates transparent executive accountability.

Revenue Cycle Performance, Cash, and Working Capital
- Analyze and lead the executive interpretation of revenue, collections, cash flow, accounts receivable aging, denials, bad debt, contractual discounts, reserves, and cost-to-collect drivers, personally working through complex or material topics.
- Build, guide, and challenge practice-level and enterprise scenario analyses that connect operational performance to cash, revenue, expense, and Adjusted Operating Profit outcomes.
- Set standards with Accounting, Controllership, RCM analytics, and practice finance for assumptions, definitions, controls, escalation thresholds, and management reporting.

Transformation, Investment, and Value Realization
- Develop and lead complex business cases and scenario models for RCM transformation programs and direct the associated financial strategy, investment requirements, benefit sizing, portfolio prioritization, performance tracking, and value realization.
- Provide senior financial leadership for billing-platform transitions, process redesign, automation, AI-enabled initiatives, and other strategic programs, resolving tradeoffs and escalating material risks.
- Establish decision-oriented scorecards and governance routines that connect initiative execution to revenue cycle, working-capital, cost, and practice outcomes.

Planning, Reporting, and Executive Communication

The Director, FP&A - HQ & IT Operating Expense provides strategic and hands-on financial leadership for Practice Management headquarters and US Oncology technology operating expense. The role owns planning, forecasting, close support, management reporting, long-range planning, and executive decision support across the full HQ and IT operating-expense portfolio. The Director connects spending, headcount, allocations, technology investments, and strategic initiatives to enterprise priorities and Adjusted Operating Profit outcomes.

The Director serves as the senior finance partner to Practice Management leaders, the McKesson technology organization, and cross-functional Finance, Accounting, Strategy, Operations, and shared-service partners. The role leads a team of three direct reports and one indirect report, establishes clear priorities and review standards, and remains directly engaged in complex analyses, executive materials, governance decisions, and issue resolution. Success requires strong executive communication, disciplined financial stewardship, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to improve processes through standardization, automation, and scalable reporting.

Key Responsibilities
Strategic FP&A Leadership and Business Partnership
- Own the financial agenda for all HQ and IT operating expense, aligning resources and investments with Practice Management, US Oncology, and enterprise priorities.
- Advise senior leaders on financial performance, choices, risks, opportunities, trade-offs, and recommended actions; translate complex cost and allocation topics into decision-ready insights.
- Lead cross-functional work across Finance, Accounting, Technology, Strategy, Operations, Ontada, McKesson Technology, and other business units to resolve issues and advance shared objectives.
- Provide concise executive storytelling for leadership reviews, forecasts, budgets, long-range planning, strategic initiatives, and emerging business issues.

Planning, Forecasting, Close, and Performance Management
- Lead annual budget planning, periodic forecasting, long-range planning, month-end close support, and management reporting for HQ and IT operating expense.
- Establish a transparent performance framework spanning employee-related expense, discretionary and semi-variable spend, technology costs, corporate and cross-business allocations, and strategic initiatives.
- Direct variance analysis, risk and opportunity assessment, headcount and open-role tracking, accrual and invoice review, and forward-looking scenario analysis.
- Ensure financial plans and reporting are accurate, well controlled, fully documented, and connected to underlying assumptions, business drivers, and Adjusted Operating Profit impact.

HQ OPEX Governance, Allocations, and Cost Stewardship
- Lead governance for retained and allocated HQ expense, including allocation methodologies, documentation, legal and contractual considerations, leadership approvals, and implementation readiness.

- Challenge new and existing spend, identify savings and cost-avoidance opportunities, and facilitate prioritization and trade-off decisions within financial targets.

Technology Finance and Investment Decision Support

Reporting, Automation, and Process Improvement

People Leadership and Organizational Effectiveness

- Set clear priorities, decision rights, service expectations, and review routines; balance effective delegation with direct engagement in urgent, ambiguous, or high-impact work.
- Build succession strength and expand team capabilities in business partnership, financial modeling, executive communication, systems, automation, and leadership.
- Foster an inclusive, collaborative, accountable culture that encourages thoughtful challenge, continuous learning, and sustainable ways of working.

Minimum Requirement
Degree or equivalent experience. Typically requires 12+ years of professional experience and 4+ years of management experience.

Education
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related field, or equivalent related experience.
- MBA, CPA, CMA, or other relevant advanced credential preferred.

Critical Skills
- Typically 12+ years of progressive finance, FP&A, accounting, or related analytical experience, including 4+ years of management responsibility.
- Demonstrated experience leading planning, forecasting, close analysis, management reporting, financial modeling, and executive decision support in a complex organization.
- Experience partnering with senior leaders across multiple functions and influencing outcomes across organizational boundaries.
- Experience with operating-expense management, headcount planning, allocations, shared services, technology finance, or investment business cases strongly preferred.
- Healthcare services, provider economics, shared-services, or multi-entity experience preferred.

Additional Skills
- Strategic and analytical thinking combined with the ability to work directly in detailed data, financial models, reporting tools, and executive materials.
- Advanced forecasting, scenario analysis, variance investigation, business-case development, and performance-management capabilities.
- Strong understanding of income-statement, capitalization, depreciation, accrual, and allocation concepts.
- Executive communication and presence, including concise written commentary, presentations, and data visualization.
- People leadership, coaching, prioritization, delegation, conflict resolution, and talent development.
- Cross-functional partnership, change leadership, sound judgment, attention to detail, ownership, and comfort operating through ambiguity.
- Digital fluency and a continuous-improvement mindset, including scalable reporting, automation, and responsible use of AI-enabled tools.

Systems and Tools
- Advanced Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint skills required.
- Experience with enterprise planning, ERP, business intelligence, and data platforms such as BPC, Essbase, SAP, PeopleSoft, Power BI, Tableau, or comparable tools preferred.

About the Role
The Senior Manager, M&A Finance Integration supports the financial planning, execution, and integration of mergers and acquisitions. Partnering with Finance leadership and cross-functional stakeholders, this role develops financial integration strategies, evaluates transaction and operational risks, supports due diligence, and helps acquired businesses transition to McKesson’s financial processes and systems.
The Senior Manager will oversee finance integration activities across the transaction lifecycle, from pre-close planning through Day 1 readiness and post-close value realization. The role requires strong experience in financial modeling, M&A due diligence, post-merger integration, and executive-level communication.

What You’ll Do
Pre-Close Planning and Due Diligence
- Develop financial integration strategies, roadmaps, governance processes, and readiness plans aligned with transaction objectives.
- Build and evaluate financial models related to integration costs, working capital, synergies, cost savings, and value realization.
- Review historical and projected financial statements, physician compensation arrangements, and operational assumptions.
- Assess target-company financial processes, systems, controls, and reporting capabilities to identify integration risks and dependencies.
- Support financial due diligence and provide input into transaction structures, commercial arrangements, and integration plans.
- Partner with Corporate Development, Operations, Legal, HR, Tax, Compliance, and other stakeholders to address financial and operational risks.

Day 1 and Post-Close Integration
- Lead finance workstreams and readiness activities supporting successful Day 1 execution.
- Establish processes for financial reporting, internal controls, cash management, revenue recognition, expense management, and physician compensation.
- Support the transition of acquired businesses onto McKesson’s financial systems, reporting platforms, and operating processes.
- Manage integration budgets, timelines, risks, dependencies, and deliverables.
- Track synergy capture, cost savings, integration performance, and value-realization milestones.
- Partner with Business Unit Finance, Operations, and IT to align forecasting, reporting, analytics, and financial planning.
- Support post-close financial reviews and audits and identify opportunities to improve future integration processes.

Governance and Executive Communication
- Establish integration KPIs, dashboards, governance routines, and escalation processes.
- Lead cross-functional finance integration meetings and communicate progress, decisions, and risks.
- Translate complex financial and operational information into clear recommendations for senior leaders.
- Influence stakeholders across functions to resolve integration issues and maintain accountability.

- Degree or equivalent and typically requires 7 or more years of relevant experience .

- Experience reviewing financial statements and assessing financial or operational risks.
- Experience managing multiple cross-functional projects, workstreams, or transaction-related deliverables.
- Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and financial planning, reporting, or analytics tools.

Preferred Skills/Experience
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related field.
- MBA, CPA, CFA, or other relevant advanced degree or certification.

- Knowledge of synergy tracking, working capital, revenue recognition, physician compensation, tax considerations, and regulatory compliance.
- Experience developing executive presentations, integration dashboards, and KPI reporting.

Description de poste
Responsable des opérations, soutien et maintenance des solutions et gestion des fournisseurs
Résumé du poste (Objectif du poste)
Le ou la Responsable des opérations, soutien et maintenance des solutions et gestion des fournisseurs assure la stabilité, la fiabilité et l’évolution continue des solutions technologiques en production dans les domaines applicatifs qui lui sont assignés. Ce rôle est responsable d’assurer l’excellence des opérations quotidiennes tout en pilotant les initiatives d’amélioration continue, d’automatisation et d’optimisation des processus afin d’améliorer l’efficacité opérationnelle, la résilience des services et l’expérience des utilisateurs.
Agissant comme leader opérationnel stratégique, cette personne identifie de façon proactive les problèmes systémiques, dirige les analyses de causes fondamentales et met en œuvre des améliorations durables afin de moderniser les modèles de soutien, de maintenance et de gestion des fournisseurs. Le poste collabore étroitement avec les équipes d’affaires, les partenaires technologiques, les fournisseurs externes et la direction afin d’assurer une prestation de services stable, sécuritaire et alignée sur les objectifs de l’entreprise.

Responsabilités clés
Soutien des solutions et opérations
- Assurer la supervision des activités quotidiennes de soutien applicatif en garantissant la stabilité, la disponibilité et la performance des systèmes en production.
- Diriger les processus de gestion des incidents, des problèmes et des changements, incluant les analyses des causes fondamentales et la mise en œuvre de mesures correctives et préventives.
- Assurer la résolution rapide et transparente des incidents en fonction des priorités d’affaires et de l’impact client.
- Définir, surveiller et communiquer les indicateurs de performance opérationnelle, la santé des services et les tendances liées aux incidents.
- Identifier les problèmes récurrents, les lacunes de processus et les faiblesses systémiques, puis diriger les initiatives visant à prévenir leur récurrence.

Maintenance, mises à niveau et amélioration continue
- Planifier, coordonner et superviser les activités de maintenance, de mise à jour, de correctifs et de remédiation des solutions supportées.
- Mettre en œuvre des opportunités d’automatisation afin de réduire les interventions manuelles et d’améliorer la fiabilité des services.
- Tirer parti des données, des outils technologiques et des capacités d’intelligence artificielle afin d’améliorer les processus opérationnels et la prise de décision.
- Évaluer et moderniser continuellement les pratiques de soutien et de maintenance pour accroître l’efficacité opérationnelle et la capacité d’évolution.
- Veiller à l’alignement des activités de maintenance avec les priorités d’affaires, les contraintes opérationnelles et les exigences de gestion des risques.
- Réduire les incidents récurrents, la dette technique et les risques opérationnels grâce à des initiatives d’amélioration continue.
- Assurer la conformité des applications aux exigences de sécurité, de réglementation, de risque et d’audit.

Gestion des fournisseurs et prestataires de services

- Assurer le respect des contrats, des ententes de niveaux de service (SLA), des ententes opérationnelles (OLA) et des normes éthiques.

- Évaluer la performance des fournisseurs à l’aide de revues de services, d’indicateurs et de mesures opérationnelles.
- Coordonner la participation des fournisseurs lors des incidents majeurs, des analyses de causes fondamentales, des maintenances et des mises à niveau.

Leadership et gouvernance opérationnelle

- Promouvoir une culture de responsabilisation, d’intégrité, de collaboration et d’amélioration continue.

The Operations Lead, Solution Support and Maintenance & Vendor Management is accountable for the stability, reliability, and continuous evolution of production solutions across assigned application domains. Acting as a strategic operational leader, the incumbent proactively identifies systemic issues, leads root cause resolution efforts, and modernizes support, maintenance, and vendor engagement practices. Solution Support & Operations
- Oversee day-to-day application support operations, ensuring production stability, availability, and performance.

- Establish, monitor, and report on operational KPIs, service health metrics, and incident trends.

Maintenance, Upgrades & Continuous Improvement
- Plan, coordinate, and oversee maintenance activities, patches, upgrades, and remediation initiatives across supported applications.
- Implement automation opportunities to reduce manual effort, improve reliability, and accelerate issue detection and resolution.

- Lead vendor vulnerability management activities, including remediation tracking, risk escalation, and issue resolution.

Financial & Business Management

Safety & Compliance

- Review incident trends and implement corrective and preventive actions.
- Lead investigations involving workplace injuries, near misses, product incidents, and compliance concerns.

Leadership & Talent Development

Continuous Improvement

- Drive improvements in productivity, quality, inventory accuracy, service performance, and employee engagement.
- Utilize data and operational metrics to identify opportunities and measure results.
- Partner with Engineering, Quality, and Inventory Control teams to improve processes and eliminate waste.
- Implement sustainable solutions that improve throughput, compliance, and customer satisfaction.

Qualifications
Required Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Logistics, Business, Operations Management, or related field preferred; equivalent experience considered.
- 5+ years of progressive leadership experience in warehouse, distribution, logistics, manufacturing, or supply chain operations.

- Strong knowledge of inventory management, warehouse operations, transportation, and material handling systems.
- Demonstrated experience managing operational metrics, budgets, labor planning, and customer service performance.
- Experience leading continuous improvement and process optimization initiatives.
- Strong communication, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
- Proficiency with Warehouse Management Systems (WMS), inventory management tools, and Microsoft Office applications.

Schedule

- Wednesday – Saturday, 7:00 AM start

- Must maintain flexibility to support multiple shifts, weekends, holidays, and changing business requirements.

- Regular leadership presence within warehouse, refrigerated, freezer, and ultra-low temperature environments ranging from -20°C to -30°C .

- Frequent walking, standing, and facility inspections across operational areas.

Position Summary

The Program Manager, New Hire Experience will lead the design, standardisation, delivery, and continuous improvement of the end-to-end experience for new colleagues joining McKesson. The role will coordinate multiple interdependent workstreams across Human Resources, hiring leaders, Facilities, Asset Management, Technology Support, Security, and other enterprise partners to ensure new hires are welcomed, equipped, connected, and productive from the outset.

This is a hands-on, highly visible role requiring strong programme leadership, executive presence, and the ability to create accountability and drive outcomes through influence in a complex, matrixed organisation. The role will establish clear governance, remove delivery barriers, and use data and colleague feedback to improve the quality, consistency, and efficiency of the new hire journey.

Main Responsibilities

• Lead a cross-functional New Hire Experience programme with multiple parallel workstreams, milestones, dependencies, and stakeholder groups.

• Create and maintain an enterprise view of the end-to-end new hire journey, from accepted offer through onboarding, initial enablement, and transition into the role.

• Drive execution, issue resolution, decision-making, and escalation in a fast-paced, people-centred environment.

• Standardise onboarding playbooks, workflows, service expectations, roles, responsibilities, and hand-offs across participating teams.

• Coordinate readiness across workspace, access, devices, equipment, systems, orientation, communications, manager preparation, and colleague support.

• Establish governance forums, delivery cadences, reporting, decision rights, escalation paths, and clear ownership of outcomes.

• Define meaningful measures of experience, readiness, timeliness, quality, and operational performance, and use insights to prioritise improvement.

• Provide senior leaders with concise, evidence-based reporting on progress, risks, decisions, outcomes, and improvement opportunities.

• Embed continuous improvement by gathering feedback from new hires, hiring managers, and delivery partners and translating findings into action.

• Promote an inclusive, accessible, and consistent experience that supports colleagues across roles, locations, and business functions.

Key Accountabilities

Programme Leadership and Execution

• Own the integrated programme plan, roadmap, milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, and benefits tracking.

• Coordinate work across multiple teams without direct authority, maintaining momentum and ensuring commitments are understood and delivered.

• Identify gaps that could affect a new hire's readiness or experience and drive timely resolution with the accountable owner.

• Prepare programme updates, decision papers, executive briefings, and recommendations for governance and leadership forums.

• Balance immediate operational needs with longer-term process, service, and experience improvements.

New Hire Journey Design and Standardisation

• Assess current onboarding practices and identify variation, duplication, delays, unclear ownership, and improvement opportunities.

• Define a consistent end-to-end New Hire Experience framework, including journey stages, service standards, control points, and expected outcomes.

• Develop and maintain practical playbooks, workflows, checklists, communications, templates, and operating procedures.

• Clarify roles, responsibilities, inputs, outputs, and hand-offs across all teams involved in enabling a new colleague.

• Ensure solutions are scalable while allowing for appropriate business, role, location, and regulatory requirements.

Cross-Functional Coordination

• Partner with Human Resources and People Leaders on pre-boarding, orientation, policies, manager readiness, colleague communications, and the overall onboarding experience.

• Coordinate with Asset Management and Technology Support on device, equipment, account, application, and access readiness.

• Partner with Facilities, Security, and relevant site teams on workspace, building access, badges, and location-specific readiness where applicable.

• Engage business, technology, procurement, learning, and other partners where their services form part of the new hire journey.

• Maintain a clear accountability model so each stakeholder understands deliverables, timing, dependencies, and escalation expectations.

Governance, Measurement and Continuous Improvement

• Establish appropriate governance, meeting cadences, working groups, decision logs, and escalation routes.

• Define and monitor measures for operational readiness, cycle time, service quality, colleague experience, issue volume, and resolution.

• Use quantitative and qualitative feedback to identify root causes, prioritise interventions, and validate whether changes improve outcomes.

• Maintain transparent reporting and ensure leaders have clear visibility of delivery status, material risks, decisions required, and realised improvements.

• Promote disciplined adoption of agreed processes and work with partners to sustain improvements over time.

Stakeholder and Executive Engagement

• Act as the central point of programme accountability for New Hire Experience outcomes.

• Build productive relationships with senior leaders, functional owners, hiring managers, and delivery teams across the organisation.

• Lead discussions, resolve conflicting priorities, and escalate material issues with clarity, judgement, and appropriate urgency.

• Communicate complex information in a concise, audience-appropriate manner and translate decisions into clear actions and ownership.

Required Skills and Experience

• 4 + years of programme or project management experience in large, complex enterprise environments.

• Demonstrated experience leading enterprise onboarding, employee experience, service delivery, operational transformation, or another complex people-centred programme.

• Proven ability to manage cross-functional programmes, dependencies, and outcomes without direct authority.

• Strong executive presence and the ability to influence senior stakeholders, facilitate decisions, and navigate competing priorities.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including executive reporting and presentation development.

• Strong organisational, analytical, problem-solving, and risk-management capabilities.

• Experience defining governance, operating models, process documentation, service measures, and continuous-improvement plans.

• Ability to work independently, demonstrate sound judgement, and deliver measurable outcomes in an evolving environment.

• Proficiency with Microsoft 365 tools used for collaboration, planning, analysis, reporting, and communication.

Preferred Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.

• Programme or project management certification.

• Change management, Lean, Six Sigma, service management, or operational excellence experience.

• Experience supporting graduate, rotational, early-career, or high-volume onboarding programmes.

• Experience working within healthcare, technology, financial services, or another large, regulated multinational organisation.

• Experience using employee feedback, operational data, and service metrics to improve colleague journeys and business outcomes.

Behavioural Competencies

Programme Leadership: Creates clarity, structure, pace, and accountability across complex, interdependent work.

Customer and Colleague Focus: Designs solutions around the needs of new hires, hiring managers, and service partners.

Influence: Builds alignment and drives decisions through credibility, evidence, and strong stakeholder relationships.

Accountability: Takes ownership of outcomes, follows through on commitments, and addresses delivery gaps directly.

Collaboration: Connects teams and functions around shared objectives, clearly defined responsibilities, and effective hand-offs.

Continuous Improvement: Uses data, feedback, and root-cause analysis to simplify processes and improve quality, consistency, and efficiency.

Communication: Provides concise, transparent, and audience-appropriate updates, recommendations, and escalations.

Adaptability: Operates effectively amid ambiguity, changing priorities, and evolving organisational needs.

What Success Looks Like

• The end-to-end new hire journey is clearly defined, documented, and consistently executed.

• New colleagues receive the information, access, equipment, support, and connections they need at the appropriate point in their journey.

• Cross-functional teams operate with clear ownership, effective hand-offs, transparent service expectations, and timely escalation.

• Risks, delays, and recurring issues are identified early, addressed decisively, and reduced through sustainable process improvements.

• Senior leaders have clear visibility into programme progress, decisions, experience measures, operational performance, and outcomes.

• Feedback from new hires, hiring managers, and delivery partners is routinely converted into prioritised improvements.

Why This Role Is Important

A colleague's early experience shapes their connection to McKesson, confidence in the organisation, and ability to contribute effectively. By bringing together the teams, processes, services, and decisions that support new hires, the Program Manager, New Hire Experience will help deliver a more consistent, efficient, and welcoming journey while strengthening accountability and operational performance across the enterprise.

jobs.title: Senior Business Intelligence & Automation Analyst
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

The Senior Business Intelligence Analyst is a highly visible, hands-on individual contributor responsible for building and scaling AIM28's analytics, reporting, and value-realization measurement capabilities. Reporting to the AIM28 Finance Lead, this role will design and own end-to-end data models, ETL pipelines, dashboards, and automation solutions that transform complex, fragmented data into trusted insights for executives and program leaders. In addition, this role will support other strategic projects as required.

The ideal candidate combines deep technical expertise in SQL, data modeling, BI visualization, automation, and AI-enabled analytics with strong business and finance acumen. Operating as the sole analytics builder within the AIM28 Finance team, this person will create the program's single source of truth for KPI, benefit, investment, and value-realization reporting while driving self-service analytics, reporting automation, and AI-powered insights across the AIM28 portfolio.

The Senior Business Intelligence Analyst will lead the development of business intelligence, data visualization, analytics, and reporting automation for the AIM28 program and other strategic projects within U.S. Pharmaceutical Distribution (USPD). AIM28 is McKesson’s AI-enabled transformation program, organized around a portfolio of Big Bets, each accountable for delivering measurable business outcomes. This role reports directly into the Sr. Director, Finance (AIM28). This role is the hands-on builder who turns Big Bet data into trusted, automated benefit and value-realization reporting for program leadership and senior executives. The source material varies: some data arrives raw and needs business logic before anyone can use it, some lives in manual files, and some is already visualized in dashboards the business teams built for themselves.

You will architect an AI-ready analytics and reporting model that pairs traditional dashboards with AI capabilities such as automated narratives and conversational agents, so stakeholders can self-serve and get to insight faster. Where data is raw, you will establish the transformation logic that makes it consumable. Where reporting lives in manual files or scattered dashboards, you will integrate and standardize it into Big Bet and AIM28 program-level solutions. This is a highly visible individual contributor role. We are looking for a builder with deep SQL proficiency, strong knowledge of data design, and the visualization and storytelling skill to brief senior executives. Expect problems to show up half-defined; your job is to turn them into reliable numbers and clear answers.

This role works under the direction of the AIM28 Finance Lead partnering with, Big Bet teams, the transformation office, and McKesson Technology to codify KPI definitions and benefit methodologies into governed data models. The goal is one version of the truth across the program.

This is a pure individual-contributor role embedded in Finance, not a role inside a BI or data engineering organization. There is no bench of other BIEs, analytics engineers, or data engineers to hand design, build, or troubleshooting off to, you own the full stack yourself, end to end. Because the role sits in Finance rather than Technology, you should also be comfortable working fluently in financial concepts: ROI, forecasting, variance-to-plan, and business-case logic, gained through direct experience partnering with a business finance or FP&A team.

What You’ll Do

Program & Big Bet reporting
- Design, build, and maintain the AIM28 program-level and Big Bet-level dashboards that track KPIs, benefits, investments, milestones, and value realization. These dashboards are the single source of truth for program performance.

- Develop executive-facing reporting for monthly Steering Committee meetings, business reviews, and leadership updates. Translate complex program data into insights leaders can act on.

Reporting automation
- Automate recurring benefit and program reporting end to end. Replace manual, file-based processes with scheduled data flows that are validated and monitored.

- Find and implement automation opportunities across reporting workflows, including AI capabilities such as automated narratives and summaries that surface insights before anyone asks for them.

Data engineering & transformation
- Build and maintain scalable ETL/ELT pipelines that extract, transform, and clean large, multi-dimensional datasets from multiple sources. These pipelines power the automated Big Bet and AIM28 program-level reporting.

- Ingest and integrate data from Big Bet teams into harmonized, consumable datasets and data models. Sources include raw operational data, manually maintained files, and dashboards the business built for itself.

- Establish the business logic that converts raw source data into certified reporting. Document the logic, lineage, and metric definitions well enough that someone else could audit or maintain the work.

- Design semantic models and curated datasets that people consume today through dashboards and self-service, and that AI agents can consume over time.

KPI & benefit frameworks
- Partner with the AIM28 Finance lead to codify KPI definitions and benefit-realization methodologies into governed data models, so measurement stays consistent across Big Bets.

- Develop and monitor the KPIs that drive business decisions. Implement data-quality checks, reconciliation, and anomaly detection to protect trust in the numbers.

Deep-dive analysis & insights
- Conduct deep-dive analyses of KPI movements, benefit variances, and program performance questions. Identify root causes and bring conclusions and recommendations to senior leadership.

- Answer ad hoc analytical questions from program leadership and Big Bet teams. When sources disagree, triangulate across them to validate data fidelity.

Self-service & adoption
- Enable governed self-service analytics for program and Big Bet stakeholders, so fewer questions turn into ad hoc requests or one-off analyses.

- Own delivery end to end, from requirements and solution design through build, UAT, and adoption. Work with business stakeholders, data engineering, and IT to keep solutions compliant with enterprise data standards.

Continuous improvement & influence
- Prioritize the reporting and automation backlog by business impact and effort. Keep stakeholders current on the roadmap and the trade-offs behind it.

- Set the standard for analytics practice (data integrity, documentation, versioning) across Big Bet teams, and coach business analysts who build their own reporting.

What You Bring

- A builder’s mindset. You take loosely defined problems, work out the business intent behind them, and deliver working solutions end to end: requirements, data model, pipeline, dashboard, adoption.

- Comfort with ambiguity and imperfect data. Raw extracts, manual spreadsheets, inconsistent definitions, and shifting requirements are the starting point here, not a blocker.

- Business acumen and financial literacy. You understand core finance concepts, ROI, forecasting, variance-to-plan, business-case logic well enough to hold your own in a finance conversation, not just translate what finance tells you. You have worked directly with a finance or FP&A team before, and you can sit with finance and business partners, understand benefit logic and business cases, and translate between data and business needs.

- Comfort as a standalone technical IC. This role sits in Finance, not in a BI or data engineering organization. There is no dedicated BIE team, data engineering bench, or technical manager to lean on for design review, code review, or troubleshooting, you are the technical function for AIM28 reporting. You are comfortable being the only builder in the room and owning decisions end to end.

- A KPI and automation track record. You have developed and monitored KPIs that drive business decisions, and you have built automated reporting systems that replaced manual processes.

- Executive presence. You have experience communicating and presenting analytical results to senior leadership, in writing and in person.

- Ownership and judgment. You validate your own outputs, make pragmatic build-versus-reuse trade-offs, and earn trust by being right about the numbers.

- Organization and prioritization. You manage multiple concurrent workstreams across Big Bets without letting deliverables or timelines slip.

- Curiosity about AI. You are interested in applying GenAI and agents to reporting, and ideally you have already experimented with them.

Technical Skills

- Expert SQL: complex query development, window functions, and performance tuning on large, multi-dimensional datasets from multiple sources. You write queries that need little post-processing.

- Data modeling and design: dimensional and star-schema modeling, semantic model design, and harmonized dataset construction. You can evaluate an end-to-end data design for its strengths and weaknesses.

- BI and visualization: advanced Power BI and Tableau, including data modeling, DAX, executive-grade dashboards, and workspace and access management.

- ETL/ELT and pipelines: hands-on experience programming to extract, transform, and clean large datasets, and building scheduled, monitored pipelines in tools such as Databricks, Microsoft Fabric, Azure Data Factory, or Snowflake.

- Scripting for automation: proficiency in Python or a similar language for data transformation and automation.

- Workflow automation: Power Automate, Power Apps, or comparable low-code tooling for reporting workflows. Exposure to modernizing legacy RPA into AI-enabled solutions is a plus.

- Analytics foundations: descriptive statistics, trend and variance analysis, and metric calibration, plus enough familiarity with inferential methods to know when to use them.

Relevant de la Directrice Principale, Gestion de la performance de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et gouvernance, le/la Gestionnaire principal(e), Gouvernance et optimisation du portefeuille est responsable de la gouvernance, des analyses de performance et du soutien à la prise de décision pour les leviers détenus par les Opérations d’approvisionnement. Le rôle assure une supervision intégrée de la performance des niveaux de service, de la gouvernance du cycle de vie des fournisseurs et des produits, de l’optimisation du portefeuille et de l’habilitation logistique, tout en garantissant une exécution rigoureuse, l’intégrité des données et une visibilité adéquate pour la direction.

Le poste établit et opère des cadres de gouvernance soutenant l’intégration des fournisseurs, les processus d’inscription et de retrait des produits, ainsi que les décisions liées au cycle de vie des produits, tout en traduisant des intrants opérationnels et analytiques complexes en informations claires et prêtes pour les décideurs exécutifs. Grâce à une collaboration transversale étroite avec les équipes de Planification, d’Approvisionnement stratégique, de Logistique entrante, des Opérations des centres de distribution, des TI et d’Analytique, le/la Gestionnaire principal(e) anticipe les risques, mène l’amélioration continue et assure l’alignement entre la gouvernance, l’exécution et les engagements en matière de niveau de service.

Section A – Responsabilités spécifiques
Performance du niveau de service et habilitation de la gouvernance
- Assurer la responsabilité des analyses de performance, des indicateurs et de la gouvernance liés aux leviers d’exécution et au niveau de service, en identifiant les risques, les tendances et les opportunités d’amélioration structurelle dans le périmètre sous responsabilité.
- Anticiper de façon proactive les impacts sur le niveau de service découlant des décisions des Opérations d’approvisionnement et définir, en partenariat avec la Planification, la Logistique entrante et les Opérations des centres de distribution, des plans d’atténuation fondés sur l’analyse des données.
- Traduire des analyses complexes en messages clairs et prêts pour les exécutifs, en présentant les arbitrages, les causes fondamentales et des recommandations appuyées par les données afin de soutenir la prise de décision de la haute direction de la chaîne d’approvisionnement.
- Définir et opérationnaliser un modèle de gouvernance de la performance pour les Opérations d’approvisionnement, incluant les définitions des KPI, la cadence de reddition de comptes, les mécanismes d’escalade et les forums de revue avec la direction.
- Collaborer avec les équipes TI et Analytique pour améliorer les rapports, tableaux de bord et la visibilité de la performance, soutenant ainsi la gouvernance, les revues de leadership et la qualité durable des décisions.

Gestion et gouvernance du cycle de vie des fournisseurs
- Définir et faire évoluer les cadres de gouvernance soutenant l’inscription et l’intégration des fournisseurs.
- Assurer l’alignement des activités liées au cycle de vie des fournisseurs avec les stratégies globales de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et de l’entreprise.
- Identifier et piloter des opportunités de simplification visant à réduire la complexité opérationnelle et à renforcer les contrôles.
- Faciliter la coordination et la communication entre l’équipe de gouvernance des fournisseurs, la Planification de l’approvisionnement et les équipes de Stratégie d’approvisionnement.
- Superviser le respect des politiques de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, des obligations contractuelles et des normes de conformité.
- Agir comme point d’escalade pour les enjeux liés aux fournisseurs et assurer leur résolution rapide via des mécanismes de gouvernance structurés.
- Promouvoir une culture d’agilité, de responsabilisation et d’innovation au sein de la fonction de gouvernance des fournisseurs et auprès des parties prenantes clés.

Gestion et gouvernance du portefeuille et du cycle de vie des produits
- Assurer une supervision stratégique des processus d’inscription et de retrait des produits afin de garantir l’alignement avec les objectifs du portefeuille et les capacités des fournisseurs.
- Mettre en place et maintenir des cadres de gouvernance permettant une exécution cohérente, efficace et conforme des activités d’inscription et de retrait.
- Assurer une coordination transversale étroite avec les équipes telles que la Gestion des catégories, la Planification de l’approvisionnement, les Ventes et la Stratégie d’approvisionnement afin de soutenir des transitions fluides et de minimiser les perturbations.
- Surveiller et valider l’exactitude des données relatives aux dossiers produits, en assurant des mises à jour en temps opportun dans les systèmes et une visibilité complète à travers la chaîne d’approvisionnement.
- Soutenir la prise de décision en révisant les propositions d’inscription et de retrait, en évaluant les impacts opérationnels et en assurant l’alignement avec les stratégies globales de l’entreprise et de la chaîne d’approvisionnement.
- Identifier et atténuer les risques opérationnels, mener des analyses post‑mortem et mettre en œuvre des plans d’action.
- Identifier des opportunités d’amélioration des processus afin de simplifier les flux de travail, réduire la complexité et accroître la réactivité face aux changements d’affaires.

Gouvernance et pilotage logistique
- Surveiller et soutenir l’exécution des activités liées aux allocations fournisseurs, à la disponibilité des produits et à l’intégrité des données dans les systèmes.
- Fournir l’orientation et la supervision nécessaires pour assurer une gestion exacte et ponctuelle des données produits et fournisseurs soutenant les opérations logistiques.
- Fournir des orientations concernant les activités de diversion des centres de distribution afin d’assurer l’alignement avec les priorités de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et les attentes en matière de niveau de service.
- Agir comme point d’escalade pour les scénarios complexes de diversion, en veillant à ce que les résolutions soutiennent les objectifs opérationnels et les engagements clients.
- Faciliter la collaboration interfonctionnelle pour résoudre les enjeux, éliminer les obstacles et assurer la cohérence des messages logistiques avec les stratégies globales de la chaîne d’approvisionnement.
- Identifier les opportunités d’amélioration des processus et soutenir la mise en œuvre de solutions visant à accroître la transparence et l’efficacité opérationnelles.

Section B – Responsabilités générales
Gestion du changement et définition de la stratégie
- Remet de façon constructive en question les façons de faire établies et contribue à identifier des pistes d’amélioration des processus; fait preuve de créativité et d’ingéniosité dans la résolution des enjeux quotidiens.
- Génère de l’engagement et de l’enthousiasme au sein des Opérations d’approvisionnement afin de soutenir l’amélioration continue.
- Considère les impacts à long terme des décisions et des actions; anticipe les tendances émergentes, les risques potentiels et les opportunités, et les communique proactivement à la direction.

Encadrement des équipes
- Dirige, encadre et développe une équipe hautement performante en favorisant une culture de responsabilisation, de collaboration et d’innovation.
- Établit des objectifs clairs, fournit une rétroaction régulière et soutient le développement de carrière.
- Soutient l’élaboration et le maintien d’un plan de relève des talents.
- Fait la promotion des valeurs de McKesson et assure un environnement de travail sécuritaire, inclusif et performant.

Section C – Exigences du poste
Expérience professionnelle
- Minimum de 9 ans d’expérience progressive en chaîne d’approvisionnement, approvisionnement ou planification, dont au moins 1 an en gestion avec responsabilité des stocks.
- Connaissance des méthodologies Lean Six Sigma ou d’amélioration continue.
- Expérience dans les biens de consommation, le commerce de détail ou l’industrie pharmaceutique est un atout.

Formation
- Baccalauréat en administration des affaires, gestion des opérations, ingénierie ou discipline connexe.
- MBA ou MSc, désignations CPIM ou SCMP sont des atouts.

Développement personnel et compétences interpersonnelles
- Solide pensée stratégique et sens des affaires et des finances.
- Capacité démontrée à diriger des équipes interfonctionnelles et à piloter des initiatives à l’échelle de l’entreprise.
- Excellentes compétences en communication, gestion des parties prenantes et leadership du changement.
- Excellentes aptitudes en collaboration et en influence.

Compétences techniques
- Connaissance des produits MS Office (PowerPoint, Excel, Word, Project, Visio).
- Connaissance de la gestion de projet.

Autres compétences et aptitudes
- Bilinguisme (anglais et français).
- Expérience solide avec la haute direction et les cadres exécutifs.
- Expérience solide dans la direction de projets stratégiques et opérationnels interfonctionnels.
- Souci du détail tout en ayant une capacité de synthèse.
- Capacité à identifier les enjeux opérationnels et stratégiques et à proposer des solutions.
- Capacité à identifier des opportunités d’amélioration et à élaborer un plan d’exécution.

Job Summary
Reporting to the Senior Director, Supply Chain Management and Governance, the Sr. Manager, Governance & Portfolio Optimization is accountable for defining and operating governance models that structure how Procurement Operations decisions are made and executed. The role owns service level insight and enablement, supplier and product lifecycle governance, portfolio optimization, and logistics enablement, ensuring decisions are disciplined, data‑driven, and aligned with enterprise priorities.

A core focus of the role is enabling product availability and logistics decisions in constrained supply environments. This includes providing governance and oversight related to manufacturer supply limitations, product availability rules, shipment quantity restrictions, and inventory flow decisions across distribution centers. The Sr. Manager establishes clear decision frameworks and escalation paths to ensure trade‑offs between service, capacity, and supply constraints are visible, understood, and consistently applied.

The role works across Supply Chain Planning, Strategic Sourcing, Distribution Centers, Inbound, IT, and Analytics teams to structure operational inputs, surface risks, and present clear decision options to leadership. It ensures governance decisions are translated into actionable direction and consistently applied across execution.

Section A – Specific Responsibilities
Service Level Performance & Governance Enablement
- Owns performance insight, analytics, and governance for service level and execution levers, identifying risks, trends, and structural improvement opportunities within scope.
- Proactively anticipates service level driven by Procurement Operations decisions, defining analytics‑driven mitigation plans in partnership with Planning, Inbound, and DC Operations.
- Translates complex analysis into clear, executive‑ready insights, articulating trade‑offs, root causes, and data‑backed recommendations to support Supply Chain leadership decision‑making.
- Defines and operationalizes a Procurement Operations performance governance model, including KPI definitions, reporting cadence, escalation paths, and leadership review forums.
- Partners with IT and BI Analytics teams to enhance reporting, dashboards, and performance visibility, supporting governance, leadership reviews, and sustained decision quality.
- May be assigned to priority enterprise initiatives and act as a project manager for the Procurement Operations Department.

Supplier Lifecycle Management and Governance
- Defines and evolves governance frameworks that support supplier listing and onboarding.
- Ensures alignment of supplier lifecycle activities with broader supply chain and business strategies.
- Drives simplification opportunities that reduce operational complexity and strengthen controls.
- Facilitates coordination and communication between the supplier governance team, Supply Planning, and Strategic Sourcing teams.
- Oversees adherence to supply chain policies, contractual obligations, and compliance standards.
- Acts as an escalation point for supplier-related issues and ensure timely resolution through structured governance.
- Promotes a culture of agility, accountability, and innovation within the supplier governance function and the key stakeholders.

Portfolio and Product Lifecycle Management and Governance
- Provides strategic oversight of product listing and delisting processes to ensure alignment with portfolio objectives and supplier capabilities.
- Establishes and maintain governance frameworks that support consistent, efficient, and compliant execution of listing and delisting activities.
- Ensures cross-functional coordination with teams such as Category Management, Supply Chain Planning, Sales, Master Data Management and Strategic Sourcing teams to support smooth transitions and minimize disruptions.
- Monitors and validate data accuracy related to product records, ensuring timely updates across systems and visibility throughout the supply chain.
- Supports decision-making by reviewing listing/delisting proposals, assessing operational impacts, and ensuring alignment with broader supply chain and business strategies.
- Identifies and mitigate operational risks; conduct post-mortems and implement action plans.
- Identifies process improvement opportunities to streamline workflows, reduce complexity, and enhance responsiveness to business changes.

Logistics Enablement
- Provides oversight and decision support to ensure product availability by managing and monitoring supply constraints, including manufacturer limitations, system‑driven availability rules, and shipment quantity restrictions.
- Ensures governance and accuracy of product and supplier information across systems to support effective planning, inventory readiness, and logistics decision‑making.
- Provides oversight and guidance on inventory diversion decisions across distribution centers, ensuring alignment with service level commitments and operational capacity.
- Acts as an escalation point for complex product flow and availability scenarios, ensuring resolutions align with customer commitments, operational objectives, and enterprise supply strategies.
- Partners with Supply Chain, Procurement, Distribution Centers, and commercial teams to resolve end‑to‑end logistics issues, align messaging, and remove operational barriers.
- Identifies opportunities to simplify processes, improve visibility into supply and inventory constraints, and support the implementation of improvements that increase efficiency and transparency.

Section B – General Responsibilities
Change Management & Strategy Setting
- Constructively challenges and influences status quo and identifies areas for process improvement; applies creative problem-solving and resourcefulness when everyday issues arise.
- Generates excitement with the Procurement Operations Department to create engagement and commitment to improving.
- Considers the long-term impacts of decisions and actions; spots new trends, potential problems, and opportunities early and communicates to leadership.

People Leadership
- Leads, coaches, and develops a high-performing team of supply chain professionals, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and innovation.
- Sets clear objectives, provides regular feedback, and supports career development.
- Supports the creation and maintenance of a talent succession plan.
- Promotes McKesson’s values and ensures a safe, inclusive, and high-performing team environment.

Section C – Position Requirements
Working Experience
- Minimum 9+ years of experience in supply chain management, procurement, or planning, including 1+ years in a management supervisory role.
- Wholesale or Pharmaceutical experience is an asset.

Education
- Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Operations Management, Engineering, or related discipline.
- MBA or MSc, PMP, Six Sigma, CPIM or SCMP designations are assets.

Personal Development and Soft Skills
- Strong strategic thinking and business and financial acumen.
- Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams and drive enterprise-wide initiatives.
- Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and change leadership skills.
- Excellent partnering and influential skills.

Technical Skills
- Strong experience in using MS Office products (Copilot, PowerPoint, Excel, Word, Project, Visio).
- Knowledge of project management.

Other Skills and Capabilities
- Bilingualism (English and French)
- Strong experience leading cross-functional strategic & operational projects.
- Attention to detail, whilst maintaining a strong sense of summary and ability to synthesize.
- Ability to identify operational and strategic issues and proactively drive solutions while leveraging new technologies.

jobs.title: Analyste en Intelligence d'Affaires / Business Intelligence Analyst
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

Résumé du Poste
L'Analyste en Intelligence d'Affaires réalise des analyses financières et commerciales pour des initiatives de génération de revenus. Ce rôle est impliqué dans le processus de reporting financier et fournit à l'équipe de direction et à l'équipe MS&P des informations décisionnelles en temps opportun sur la performance financière de McKesson et de ses partenaires commerciaux (fournisseurs et clients), ainsi que sur les opportunités commerciales. L'Analyste en Intelligence d'Affaires prépare des business cases solides pour de nouvelles opportunités, développe des plans financiers pour soutenir les négociations et surveille les écarts de performance. Le candidat contribuera également à la préparation de portefeuilles et d'informations clés nécessaires pour les réunions avec les fournisseurs et les clients.

Section A – Responsabilités Spécifiques
- Construit et maintient un hub de données maître des fournisseurs qui contient les termes et conditions contractuels.
- Suit le rendement des fournisseurs et d'autres indicateurs de rentabilité au fil du temps pour la modélisation financière.
- Exploite les ensembles de données pour modéliser des stratégies de négociation de manière proactive et ad hoc pour l'équipe MS&P.
- Surveille la performance des ventes des fournisseurs pour fournir des informations aux parties prenantes internes.
- Fournit à l'équipe MS&P des informations décisionnelles grâce à un reporting cohérent, des métriques et de l'intelligence d'affaires (par exemple, rentabilité des fournisseurs) sur les activités d'approvisionnement.
- Réalise des analyses génératrices de revenus – au niveau global et détaillé des fournisseurs.
- Prépare des business cases détaillés pour évaluer le rapport coût-bénéfice des achats d'opportunité et d'autres nouvelles initiatives.
- Identifie et communique les risques financiers et fournit des recommandations pour les programmes et initiatives sous-performants afin de s'assurer que les KPI restent en ligne avec les objectifs de McKesson.
- Met à jour les fichiers budgétaires, assure leur exactitude et leur intégrité, soumet ces fichiers à l'équipe de direction et participe activement aux processus de prévision financière, de budgétisation annuelle et de planification à long terme.
- Responsable du cycle de reporting de fin de mois et de l'examen des résultats financiers ; prévisions mensuelles.
- Collecte des données sur la performance financière des fournisseurs basées sur les KPI définis par l'équipe MS&P et communique les résultats pour soutenir le suivi de la gestion de la performance des fournisseurs.
- Travaille avec les équipes MS&P et des opérations d'approvisionnement, et dans certains cas, directement avec le fournisseur pour mettre en œuvre et surveiller les incitations basées sur la performance en rapport avec les métriques ou objectifs convenus.
- Mesure la croissance des revenus et la performance financière générale des achats.
- Soutient les négociations menées par MS&P en fournissant des informations significatives sur la rentabilité du fabricant et l'intelligence de marché.
- Collabore avec ses collègues Analystes d'Affaires à travers MGPS pour tirer parti des meilleures pratiques et opportunités.

Section B – Responsabilités Générales
- Maintient une connaissance pertinente des catégories de produits et se tient informé des tendances et conditions du marché et de l'industrie.
- Agit en tant qu'ambassadeur des valeurs d'entreprise de McKesson (ICARE, ILEAD).

Section C – Exigences du Poste
Expérience Professionnelle
- 3 à 5 ans d'expérience en finance, chaîne d'approvisionnement, approvisionnement, gestion des stocks et réapprovisionnement.
- Expérience en commerce de détail/gros/sciences de la vie un atout.
- Expérience en gestion des stocks un atout.

Éducation
- Diplôme de baccalauréat en administration des affaires, gestion des opérations, finance ou équivalent.

Développement Personnel et Compétences Relationnelles
- Forte compréhension des affaires et compétences analytiques.
- Leadership démontré.
- Excellentes compétences en partenariat.
- Solides compétences en communication et présentation.
- Capacité à collaborer avec différents niveaux de management et d'employés.

Compétences Techniques
- Bilingue, à l'écrit comme à l'oral.
- Maîtrise des systèmes ERP, du réapprovisionnement, IA et des systèmes SQL un atout.
- Connaissance approfondie des produits MS Office (Power BI, Power Point, Excel, Word, Project).
- Connaissance des processus financiers et d'approvisionnement de la chaîne d'approvisionnement.
- Solides compétences en modélisation financière.

Autres Compétences et Capacités
- Capacité à travailler en tant que membre d'équipes transversales.
- Sens aigu de la synthèse et capacité à synthétiser tout en étant orienté vers le détail.
- Esprit d'équipe.
- Capacité à identifier les problèmes opérationnels et stratégiques et à proposer des solutions proactives.

Job Summary
The Business Intelligence Analyst performs financial and commercial analysis for revenue generation initiatives. The role is involved in the financial reporting process and provides the management team and MS&P team with timely decision-making information on financial performance of McKesson and its business partners (vendors and clients), as well as commercial opportunities. The Business Intelligence Analyst prepares sound business cases for new opportunities, develops financial plans to support negotiations, and monitors gaps in performance. The candidate will also contribute to the preparation of portfolios and key information required for supplier and customer meetings.

Section A – Specific Responsibilities
- Builds and maintains supplier master data hub which houses contractual terms and conditions
- Tracks supplier yield and other profitability metrics over time for the purpose of financial modeling
- Leverages data sets to model negotiation strategies proactively and ad hoc for MS&P team
- Monitors supplier sales performance to provide insights to internal stakeholders
- Provides the MS&P team with decision-making information through consistent reporting, metrics and business intelligence (e. g. vendors’ profitability) on procurement activities.
- Conducts revenue generating analyses – at overall and vendor-level of detail
- Prepares detailed business cases to assess cost-benefits of opportunity buys and other new initiatives.
- Identifies and communicates financial risks and provides recommendations for low performing programs and initiatives to ensure KPIs stay in line with McKesson targets.
- Updates budget files, ensures their accuracy and integrity, submits these files to the Management team and actively participates in the financial forecasting, annual budgeting and long-range plan process.
- Responsible for month-end reporting cycle and review of financial results; monthly forecasting
- Collects data on vendors’ financial performance based on KPIs defined by the MS&P team and communicates results to support follow-up on vendor performance management.
- Works with MS&P and Procurement Operations teams, and in some cases, directly with vendor to implement and monitor performance-driven incentives pertaining to agreed-to metrics or objectives
- Measures revenue growth and general procurement financial performance.
- Supports negotiations led by MS&P by providing meaningful insights into manufacturer’s profitability and market intelligence.
- Collaborates with Business Analyst colleagues across MGPS to leverage best practices and opportunities

Section B – General Responsibilities
Other
- Maintains relevant business knowledge of product categories and stays abreast of market and industry trends and conditions.

- Acts as a McKesson ambassador of corporate values ( ICARE, ILEAD ).

Section C – Position Requirements

Work Experience
- 3-5 years of experience in finance, supply chain, procurement, inventory management and replenishment.
- Retail/Wholesale/Life Sciences experience an asset.
- Inventory management experience an asset.

Education
- Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Operations Management, Finance or equivalent.

Personal Development and Soft Skills
- Strong business acumen and analytical skills.
- Demonstrated leadership.
- Excellent partnering skills.
- Strong communication and presentation skills.
- Ability to collaborate with various levels of management and employees.

Technical Skills
- Bilingual, both written and spoken.
- Proficiency with ERP systems, replenishment, AI and SQL systems an asset.
- Extensive knowledge of MS Office products (Power BI, Power Point, Excel, Word, Project).
- Knowledge of supply chain finance and procurement processes.
- Solid financial modeling skills.

Other Skills and Capabilities
- Ability to work as part of cross-functional teams.
- Strong sense of summary and ability to synthesize, whilst being detail oriented.
- Team player.
- Ability to identify operational and strategic issues and proactively drive solutions.

The incumbent of this position will provide daily support to internal and/or external clients outside Quebec and/or in the United States. Therefore, he/she must be proficient in spoken and written English. Please note that the number of positions requiring English language skills has been limited where possible.

Veuillez noter que le nombre de postes dont les tâches requièrent une connaissance de la langue anglaise a été restreint dans la mesure du possible.

jobs.title: Lead Workforce Intelligence Researcher - Strategic Workforce Planning & Organizational Effectiveness
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

POSITION SUMMARY

Serves as the enterprise authority on workforce strategy, workforce intelligence, organization design, and organizational effectiveness. Defines the research agenda, planning frameworks, and methodologies that translate business strategy into workforce insights, future-looking scenarios, and organizational recommendations. This role incorporates AI and automation trends to help leaders understand how work, skills, roles, and structures must evolve.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Enterprise Domain Leadership

Research, Insights & Methods

• Act as the enterprise authority for strategic workforce planning, workforce intelligence, and organizational effectiveness.

• Establish methods, frameworks, and standards for workforce planning, organization diagnostics, and workforce intelligence.

• Define the strategic research agenda and proactively identify future workforce risks, opportunities, and capability needs.

• Represent Workforce Intelligence as the senior subject matter expert for workforce strategy and organizational effectiveness.

• Lead research on workforce demand, talent supply, critical roles, capabilities, skills evolution, labor market trends, and future workforce needs.

• Conduct organizational effectiveness analyses including spans and layers, operating models, work design, capacity, productivity, and organizational health.

• Develop planning scenarios, forecasts, diagnostics, and recommendations that support strategic business objectives.

• Synthesize internal workforce data, external labor market intelligence, and business context into executive-ready insights.

AI-Enabled Research & Innovation

Strategic Advisory & Influence

• Research the workforce implications of AI, automation, and emerging technologies on roles, skills, capacity, work design, and organization structures.
