Sommaire du poste
Relevant du vice-président/directeur général, Achats et Approvisionnement stratégique, le directeur principal, Achats et Approvisionnement stratégique, OTC-CPG Amérique du Nord, est un rôle de leadership clé responsable de piloter les relations commerciales avec les fournisseurs, tant au Canada qu’aux États-Unis, pour McKesson Global Procurement and Sourcing (MGPS). Ce poste dirige la stratégie de l’approvisionnement de bout en bout des dépenses commerciales liées aux canaux de vente en gros et au détail pour les catégories nationales de marques OTC-CPG en Amérique du Nord, dans le but de maximiser le rendement des fournisseurs et d’accroître la valeur commerciale pour les activités canadiennes et américaines. Le directeur principal agit comme principal point de contact commercial auprès des fournisseurs nord-américains, dirige les activités de négociation, assure l’exécution des contrats et évalue la performance des fournisseurs sur les différents marchés. Ce leader favorise l’alignement stratégique entre les équipes MGPS des deux pays ainsi qu’avec les équipes de gestion des catégories, ventes, opérations et partenaires du commerce de détail et met en œuvre des programmes qui renforcent la position concurrentielle de McKesson ainsi que ses partenariats fournisseurs.

Section A – Responsabilités spécifiques
- Définit et est responsable de la stratégie nord-américaine de l’approvisionnement OTC-CPG pour les fonds commerciaux de vente en gros et au détail, en assurant une approche unifiée entre le Canada et les États-Unis tout en respectant les dynamiques de marché et exigences réglementaires propres à chaque pays.
- Assume le rôle de chef de file commercial principal auprès des fournisseurs OTC-CPG nord- américains, en stimulant des engagements fondés sur des partenariats afin de créer une valeur mutuelle pour les activités au Canada et aux Etats-Unis.
- Dirige le cadre de l’approvisionnement conjoint pour les canaux de vente en gros et au détail, en assurant l’uniformité des approches en matière d’engagement fournisseur, de stratégies de négociations et d’optimisation des fonds commerciaux à l’échelle continentale.
- Supervise et oriente les négociations fournisseurs, incluant l’initiation, la gestion et le renouvellement des ententes de vente en gros et au détail, des coûts, des allocations fournisseurs et des conditions commerciales pour les fournisseurs opérant sur les marchés en Amérique du Nord.
- Pilote la gestion de la performance des fournisseurs en établissant des indicateurs clés de performance (KPI), en menant des revues d’affaires régulières et en assurant le suivi des objectifs financiers liés à la croissance du rendement, à la protection des marges et à la récupération des fonds commerciaux dans les deux pays.
- Agit comme principal intermédiaire auprès des activités de commerce de détail de McKesson au Canada et aux Etats-Unis, en veillant à une compréhension approfondie des besoins des
catégories, des stratégies de mise en marché et des priorités clients de toutes les bannières de détail et divisions de vente en gros.
- Fait la promotion de l’innovation commerciale en identifiant continuellement de nouvelles occasions de génération de revenus, des programmes fournisseurs et des modèles de partenariats renfonçant la proposition de valeur OTC-CPG de McKesson sur les deux marchés.
- Collabore de façon transversale avec les équipes ventes, opérations, gestion des catégories et les principaux clients de McKesson à l’échelle nord-américaine afin d’identifier et de concrétiser des occasions à valeur ajoutée issues de l’écosystème fournisseur.
- Assure l’intégralité stratégique entre les marchés MGPS en collaborant étroitement avec les collègues de l’approvisionnement au Canada et aux Etats-Unis afin d’harmoniser les meilleur pratiques, de partager l’intelligence de marché et de maintenir une cohérence dans les messages et les interactions avec les fournisseurs.

Section B – Responsabiités générales

- Établit et met en œuvre les objectifs, et favorise une culture axée sur la performance, l’amélioration continue et la collaboration avec la direction, les pairs et les subordonnés.
- Agit à titre d’ambassadeur des valeurs corporatives de McKesson.

Autres compétences et aptitudes

Position Summary:

The Payroll, Compensation & Benefits IT Specialist serves as the primary technical subject matter expert for the Dayforce HCM platform. This role leverages Dayforce’s single-instance platform to configure, maintain, and optimize core modules—including Dayforce Payroll, Total Rewards, Benefits Administration, Advanced HR, and Time & Attendance .

The ideal candidate blends deep technical capabilities (Rules Engine configuration, Data Transformations, API/Integration management) with a strong operational understanding of multi-state payroll, wage compliance, and total rewards workflows.

Key Responsibilities

1. Dayforce Module Configuration & Rules Management
- Configure, maintain, and audit system rules within Dayforce Payroll, Benefits, Compensation, and Dayforce Time & Attendance .

- Utilize the Dayforce Rules Engine to build complex earning/deduction rules, overtime calculations, shift differentials, garnishment processing, and pay policy parameters.

- Administer annual Open Enrollment within Dayforce, configuring carrier plans, eligibility rules, life events, enrollment workflows, and passive event triggers.

- Configure compensation cycles, merit matrix models, bonus structures, and eligibility criteria across various business units.

2. System Integration & Data Engineering

- Design, build, and maintain automated data exchanges using Dayforce Data Transformations (XML / XSLT) , Web Services APIs, and secure file transfers (SFTP).

- Manage 834 EDI carrier feeds, 401(k)/pension provider interface files, and custom General Ledger (GL) posting interfaces.

- Manage API connections connecting Dayforce to enterprise ERP systems, banking networks (ACH/NACHA formats), and third-party vendor applications.

3. Analytics, Reporting & Compliance

- Author, schedule, and optimize standard and complex custom reports using Dayforce Analytics / Ad-Hoc Reporting and SQL.

- Conduct regular system audits to ensure compliance with federal, state, and local labor standards (e.g., FLSA overtime rules, ACA 1095-C tracking, ERISA, and local tax requirements).

- Retrieve and prepare system logs, audit reports, and balance statements to support internal/external financial and SOC compliance audits.

4. Release Management & Tier 3 Support

- Serve as the Tier 3 escalation point for complex payroll calculation glitches, benefits transmission errors, or rule logic failures.

- Manage regression testing and validation during Dayforce Service Packs, weekly release updates, and yearly tax table updates .

- Oversee Dayforce Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), Feature Access, and Data Access policies to ensure strict PII security.

Minimum Qualifications:

- Degree or equivalent and typically requires 4+ years of relevant experience.

Required Qualifications & Skills

- Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Management Information Systems (MIS), Information Technology, or equivalent practical experience.

- Experience: 4+ years of hands-on technical configuration and administration experience within the Dayforce (Ceridian) platform.

- Technical Expertise:
- Demonstrated experience configuring the Dayforce Rules Engine (Pay Setup, Benefit Setup, Compensation Setup).

- Hands-on proficiency with Data Transformations (XML, XSLT) , SFTP protocol setup, and API integrations within Dayforce.

- Expert-level custom report authoring using Dayforce Analytics .

- Functional Knowledge:
- Strong working knowledge of multi-state/multi-jurisdiction payroll processing, tax filing rules, and benefits administration logic.

- Understanding of regulatory compliance frameworks (ACA, FLSA, HIPAA, SOC 1/2).

Preferred Certifications
- Dayforce Certified Professional (e.g., Dayforce Payroll, Dayforce Benefits, or Dayforce Integration Specialist)

- CPP (Certified Payroll Professional)

- WorldatWork CCP (Certified Compensation Professional) or SHRM-CP / PHR

About McKesson Medical-Surgical

McKesson Medical-Surgical (MMS), which is expected to become Wellverse in early 2027, is a subsidiary and publicly reported segment of the McKesson Corporation. MMS distributes medical-surgical supplies, pharmaceuticals, diagnostic equipment and supplies, along with other solutions and services to virtually every type of healthcare setting and provider outside of the traditional hospital. These markets – often referred to as Alternate Care or Non-Acute Care – include physician offices, surgery centers, long-term care providers, laboratories, home health and hospice agencies, health systems, government facilities and online marketplaces and retailers.

Alternate Care markets are growing rapidly and MMS is proud to be a leader in this space. With a team of approximately 8,000 employees, a network of 15 distribution centers and approximately 900 delivery vehicles, we collaborate with more than 2,200 leading manufacturers and serve over 200,000 customer accounts across the U.S. Our catalog includes more than 270,000 SKUs of branded and private-label medical-surgical products – from bandages to specialty pharmaceuticals and COVID-19 tests.

The MMS Legal Department is seeking a Lead Counsel, Employment to join its Technology, Risk & People (TRP) pillar. This role is critical to MMS’s transition to a standalone company. The TRP team provides practical, business-oriented legal support across human resources, employee benefits, executive compensation, technology, compliance, and risk-related matters, helping the business achieve its objectives while appropriately managing legal and regulatory risk.  The role reports to the Managing Principal Counsel, Technology, Risk & People.

This position serves as a trusted legal partner providing day-to-day advice on employment, workforce, benefits, and people-related matters. The successful candidate will work closely with cross-functional stakeholders to identify and address legal risks, support key business and workforce initiatives, and help develop practical, scalable solutions that balance legal requirements with business needs. The role requires sound judgment, strong collaboration skills, a proactive mindset, and the ability to operate effectively in a dynamic environment with evolving priorities and occasional ambiguity.

The Lead Counsel is expected to serve as a strategic thought partner to senior Human Resources, Finance, Compensation, and business leaders. This individual will assess complex legal and business risks, guide high-impact workforce decisions, develop governance and compliance frameworks, and help shape long-term people-related strategies while balancing legal, regulatory, operational, and business considerations.
This position offers the opportunity to help build foundational processes and legal frameworks that support organizational growth, workforce innovation, and compliance in a newly independent healthcare company.

Key Responsibilities
- Legal Counseling: Serve as the company's lead legal advisor on labor, employment, employee benefits, and executive compensation matters, providing strategic, risk-based counsel on complex and high-profile workforce issues, organizational changes, executive matters, and enterprise initiatives.
- Ownership & Build: Lead legal support for enterprise-wide workforce, benefits, and executive compensation initiatives. Design and implement scalable legal, compliance, and governance frameworks that support organizational growth, workforce transformation, and public-company readiness. Partner across legal functions to develop coordinated enterprise risk management strategies.
- Drafting : Draft or comment on various HR, employment and benefits related agreements, policies and guidelines.
- Collaboration: Partner with HR, business leaders and cross functional leaders to proactively identify and manage labor, employment, benefits, and executive compensation risks, and implement practical, preventative solutions.
- Outside Counsel Oversight: Effectively manage outside counsel, including budgeting, scope management, and review of work product.  Partnering with Senior Litigation Counsel as appropriate.
- Execution & Adaptability: Manage competing priorities, adjust to changing business needs, and operate effectively with limited structure in certain areas.
- Regulatory Awareness: Anticipate emerging legal and regulatory developments affecting employment, benefits, executive compensation, and workforce strategy. Assess enterprise impact and lead implementation of proactive compliance and risk mitigation initiatives.

Qualifications
Minimum Requirements
- JD and active U.S. bar membership

- 10-15 years of relevant legal experience at a law firm and/or in-house legal department (preferred)

Critical Skills & Experience
- Experience with: - Employment law counseling
- HR policy development
- Benefit plan design and administration legal counseling (a plus)
- Executive compensation legal counseling (a plus)

- Demonstrated ability to independently lead complex legal matters and influence executive-level decision-making.
- Strong executive presence with the ability to advise and challenge senior leaders while maintaining trusted relationships.
- Proven ability to lead cross-functional initiatives across HR, Finance, Compliance, Internal Audit, Regulatory Affairs, and business operations.
- Working knowledge of 50 state labor and employment laws
- Working knowledge of benefits and executive compensation laws (a plus)
- Strong drafting, negotiation, and issue-spotting skills
- Strong research skills
- Ability to provide clear, practical legal guidance
- Proven ability to adapt to evolving business needs and operate effectively in ambiguous situations
- Strong collaboration and communication skills

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience in the healthcare, life sciences, pharmaceutical, medical device, healthcare technology, or healthcare distribution industries.

Additional Information

- Up to 25% travel

Authorization

McKesson Medical-Surgical (MMS), which is expected to become Wellverse in early 2027, is a subsidiary and publicly reported segment of the McKesson Corporation. MMS distributes medical-surgical supplies, pharmaceuticals, diagnostic equipment and supplies, along with other solutions and services to virtually every type of healthcare setting and provider outside of the traditional hospital. These markets – often referred to as Alternate Care or Non-Acute Care – include physician offices, surgery centers, long-term care providers, laboratories, home health and hospice agencies, health systems, government facilities and online marketplaces and retailers.

jobs.title: Vice President, HR Support Center & Operations
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

The Role

The Vice President, HR Support Center & Operations provides enterprise leadership for McKesson’s global HR support contact center and Workforce Administration operations. The role is accountable for the strategy, operating model, governance, service performance, talent, and transformation agenda across employee-facing HR support and high-volume workforce administration services.

This leader combines exceptional people leadership with deep operational discipline. The Vice President leads through senior leaders and managers, creates a culture of ownership and care, and ensures employees and leaders receive accurate, timely, consistent, and customer-centered support across geographies.

A central mandate is to define and deliver the future of HR operations. The Vice President establishes the automation, data, process, and technology foundation needed to simplify work, reduce manual effort, increase efficiency, strengthen controls, and scale consistent practices globally. The role partners closely with HR Technology and enterprise stakeholders to translate operational needs into a sequenced modernization roadmap.

As a senior HR service-delivery leader, the Vice President advises HR and business executives on employee support trends, service demand, capacity, operational risk, workforce needs, process performance, and investment priorities. The role builds strong partnerships across Employee Care, HR Centers of Excellence, HR Business Partners, HR Technology, Payroll, Legal, Finance, and other enterprise functions.

Organizational Scope

- Global HR support contact center, including employee and leader inquiry, case, and escalation management

- Workforce Administration / HR Operations teams responsible for employee lifecycle transactions, records, data changes, and related operational services

- Service management, workforce planning, quality, knowledge, reporting, governance, and continuous improvement capabilities supporting the portfolio

- Global process standardization, automation, digital enablement, and technology modernization for HR service delivery

- Leadership Model: The Vice President is accountable for enterprise strategy, global integration, governance, performance, resource direction, transformation, and talent across the portfolio. Operational leaders and subject-matter experts retain accountability for detailed process design, technical decisions, and day-to-day execution within their areas.

Key Responsibilities

- Enterprise Strategy and Operating Model

- - Establish and execute a multi-year global strategy for the HR Support Center and Workforce Administration organization, aligned with enterprise HR priorities and business objectives.
- Design an integrated operating model that clarifies global, regional, and local responsibilities, decision rights, service boundaries, escalation paths, and accountability.
- Set the vision for a scalable, employee-centered service organization that balances experience, quality, speed, risk, cost, and global consistency.
- Translate enterprise HR strategy, workforce needs, and service insights into prioritized operating plans, capability investments, and measurable outcomes.
- Advise senior HR and business leaders on service trends, operational risks, capacity, organizational capability, and investment needs.

- Global Service Delivery and Operational Performance - Lead reliable, accurate, timely, and consistent delivery across the global HR support contact center and Workforce Administration teams.
- Establish common service standards, operating rhythms, performance measures, quality practices, and escalation mechanisms across geographies.
- Use demand, case, contact, transaction, quality, productivity, employee experience, and cost data to improve performance and guide decisions.
- Strengthen workforce management, capacity planning, knowledge management, quality assurance, and leader routines to meet changing demand.
- Reduce fragmentation, improve handoffs, resolve recurring service defects, and optimize the end-to-end employee and leader experience.
- Balance enterprise consistency with legal, regulatory, language, workforce, and business requirements across supported markets.

- Technology, Automation and Transformation - Define and sponsor the technology and automation vision for HR operations, creating a durable foundation for future service delivery.
- Build and maintain a sequenced transformation roadmap spanning process redesign, workflow automation, AI-enabled capabilities, knowledge, analytics, self-service, case management, and contact-center technologies.
- Partner with HR Technology, Digital, Data, Security, and enterprise teams to convert operational opportunities into scalable solutions and disciplined implementation plans.
- Identify high-value opportunities to eliminate unnecessary manual work, simplify complex processes, consolidate fragmented activity, and improve straight-through processing.
- Establish appropriate governance, controls, testing, adoption measures, and benefits realization for automation and technology investments.
- Create a continuous-improvement system that equips leaders and teams to identify root causes, test solutions, scale proven practices, and sustain results.

- Governance, Risk and Controls - Establish portfolio-level governance, policies, controls, documentation standards, and performance expectations that support consistent execution and responsible risk management.
- Maintain executive visibility into material service risks, control issues, recurring defects, employee impacts, and remediation plans.
- Partner with Legal, Cyber Security, Payroll, HR Centers of Excellence, Audit, and other experts to identify and mitigate operational, regulatory, financial, data, and employee-experience risks.
- Ensure sensitive or complex matters are routed to the appropriate experts and escalated for leadership decisions when required.
- Drive clear ownership for process controls, issue resolution, business continuity, and operational resilience.

- People and Organizational Leadership - Lead, inspire, coach, and develop a geographically distributed organization through senior leaders, managers, and subject-matter experts.
- Create an inclusive, high-performing culture grounded in care, accountability, collaboration, continuous learning, customer orientation, and operational excellence.
- Build leadership capability, organizational depth, succession readiness, and critical skills for a more digital and automated operating environment.
- Establish clear expectations and empower leaders to make decisions, remove barriers, and own outcomes.
- Assess organizational structure, roles, skills, spans, capacity, location strategy, and resource deployment as business and technology needs evolve.
- Lead teams through significant operating-model, process, and technology change with transparent communication and disciplined change leadership.

- Executive and Cross-Functional Partnership - Translate complex operational themes, service insights, risks, and investment choices into clear, decision-ready recommendations for executives.
- Influence enterprise priorities and solutions across a highly matrixed environment where direct authority may not exist.
- Represent HR support and operations requirements in enterprise planning, technology, transformation, and governance forums.
- Build productive partnerships with HR Centers of Excellence and HR Business Partners to improve policy-to-process translation and service readiness.
- Lead cross-functional initiatives requiring alignment across multiple HR disciplines, geographies, and stakeholder groups.

Qualifications
Minimum Requirements

- Typically, 15+ years of progressive experience in operations, contact centers, shared services, employee services, HR operations, business operations, or a related discipline.
- Typically, 8+ years of senior leadership experience with accountability for leaders, large or complex teams, service delivery, planning, communication, and organizational performance.
- Demonstrated experience leading operations and/or a contact center environment; experience with high-volume, multi-channel service delivery is required.
- Proven success leading geographically distributed teams through managers and senior leaders in a large, matrixed organization.
- Demonstrated ability to establish enterprise operating models, service standards, governance, performance measures, workforce plans, budgets, and resource strategies.
- Experience defining and delivering complex transformation, automation, technology, or process-optimization initiatives with measurable business outcomes.
- Strong understanding of operational risk, controls, privacy, data stewardship, compliance, and business continuity, with sound judgment about when to engage specialized experts.
- Ability to use operational data, service insights, employee feedback, and cost-benefit analysis to shape priorities and improve organizational performance.
- Executive-level communication, influence, and change-leadership skills.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with contact-center platforms, case management, knowledge management, workforce management, digital self-service, workflow, analytics, automation, and AI-enabled service capabilities.
- Experience managing outsourced services, vendor-supported operations, or strategic third-party relationships.
- Lean, Six Sigma, process excellence, service management, or change-management experience.

Critical Skills

- People leadership: Builds trust, develops exceptional leaders, creates followership, and sustains an inclusive culture of care and accountability.
- Enterprise operational leadership: Connects strategy, service delivery, workforce, governance, and investment decisions across a complex global portfolio.
- Technology and automation vision: Defines a pragmatic future-state architecture and roadmap that modernizes operations and delivers measurable value.
- Customer-centered service mindset: Designs services around employee and leader needs while maintaining accuracy, consistency, controls, and scalability.
- Transformation leadership: Mobilizes teams through operating-model, process, and technology change and converts strategy into sustained execution.
- Systems thinking: Understands how policy, process, people, technology, data, controls, and service channels interact across the employee lifecycle.
- Data-driven management: Uses performance measures, demand patterns, quality insights, risk indicators, employee feedback, and financial analysis to make decisions.
- Executive influence: Communicates clearly, frames trade-offs, and aligns senior stakeholders around decisions and outcomes.
- Global perspective: Creates enterprise consistency while respecting regional and jurisdictional requirements.
- Operational judgment: Balances employee experience, service, cost, capacity, risk, compliance, and speed in complex situations.

Education
Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent experience.

Physical Requirements
- General office demands
- Must have the ability to travel 10-20% of the time

Location
Hybrid with proximity to one of the following hub locations: Irving, TX; Alpharetta, GA; Montreal, QC; Toronto, ON

Specific in ‑ office days may be designated based on team needs and business priorities.

About the Role:

The   Sr. Director,   Segment Strategy –   Supply Chain Operations   serves as a senior individual contributor within the North America Pharmaceutical Distribution Strategy function, supporting the   Supply Chain Operations   (SC O )   segment.   SCO   represents   McKesson's robust supply chain ,   distribution operation s ,   and dedicated customer support team s ,   including   over 6,000 highly skilled associates .   Reporting to the VP,   Segment Strategy , this position   operates   as a lead strategic partner to segment leadership.

The Senior Director   is responsible for   owning and leading defined workstreams and strategic sub-areas within the segment, shaping insights, framing decisions, and driving forward progress in close partnership with business and functional leaders. This is a highly hands-on role that requires strong judgment in stakeholder engagement and a commitment to developing strategy collaboratively—not in isolation.

Success in this role is defined by the ability to translate complex dynamics into actionable decisions, build credibility with partners, and ensure strategic work leads to practical, executable outcomes.

What You'll Do:

Strategic Initiative Leadership

- Lead strategic initiatives end-to-end — from problem definition and workplan design through analysis, recommendation development, syndication, and hand-off to execution owners.

- Structure ambiguous, contested problems into clear hypotheses, workplans, and decision paths; insist on clear problem definition, logic, and evidence.

- Develop recommendations that reflect genuine choices with explicit trade-offs — not lists of initiatives — and that are grounded in the financial architecture of the relevant market.

- Prepare and run productive problem-solving sessions with business partners; engage stakeholders in joint problem solving rather than delivering conclusions to them.

Value Chain Economics & Financial Analysis

- Serve as a knowledgeable resource on the financial architecture of the pharmaceutical value chain — how manufacturers, distributors, PBMs, payers, and pharmacies generate and protect economic value, and how those mechanisms are being   repriced .

- Direct and quality-control the financial models built by the   team;   ensure every significant analysis   identifies   the assumptions that matter most and translates market shifts into quantified P&L implications.

- Analyze the second-order financial and competitive consequences of legislative and regulatory developments — drug pricing reform, PBM transparency , reimbursement   policy — within the scope of assigned initiatives.

- Contribute to scenario analysis of vertical integration, direct channel development, and disintermediation moves by value chain participants.

Thought Partnership & Syndication

- Act as a credible thought partner to business leaders within the scope of assigned initiatives; challenge assumptions constructively and surface inconvenient facts early.

- Understand the organization’s culture and individual stakeholder   perspectives, and   consider them in crafting recommendations that the business can   actually execute .

- Develop thoughtful plans to engage stakeholders through the process — from fact-finding to solution development — to build alignment as the work proceeds, not after it concludes.

Communication

- Deliver compelling written and oral communications to senior business audiences; lead with key messages, present persuasively and with conviction, and tailor materials to the audience.

- Ask powerful, open-ended questions; actively listen and respond to nuance and mood in senior settings.

Team Leadership & Development

- Partner with and direct teams of one to three Senior Managers and analysts per initiative; scope   work   realistically against team capacity and deliver high-quality output without undue crunch.

- Coach team members in a   strengths -based way; provide insightful,   timely   feedback; shape step-up opportunities that stretch colleagues.

- Contribute to a positive, inclusive team climate and to function-building efforts including recruiting and knowledge development.

Execution Support

- Translate approved recommendations into   implementation   roadmaps with clear owners, milestones, and metrics; support transformation programs through their early execution phases.

- Create feedback loops that surface early execution signals back into   the strategic   logic.

Basic   Requirements:

- 10+ years of progressive experience in strategy, including engagement-leadership experience at a top-tier strategy consulting firm or equivalent project-leadership experience in a corporate strategy function.

- 5+ years of e xperience in distribution   supply chain ; strong preference for pharmaceutical and/or healthcare   distribution   experience.

- Demonstrated ability to build working fluency in complex value chain economics quickly.

- Track record   of leading cross-functional strategic projects end-to-end that resulted in concrete decisions and measurable action — not just analysis delivered to others.

- Demonstrated ability to lead and develop small analytical teams.

- Executive presence and   demonstrated   effectiveness   presenting to   and influencing senior leaders.

Preferred Skills/Experience:

- Problem Framer:   Structures problems soundly using core problem-solving disciplines; translates ambiguity into hypotheses, workplans, and decision paths; embraces qualitative, people, and relationship-based problem solving alongside the quantitative.

- Value Chain Fluency:   Possesses   working knowledge of pharmaceutical value chain economics — distribution margin structures, sourcing dynamics, PBM and payer economics, and pharmacy P&Ls — and applies it as a core analytical lens, not background knowledge.

- Recommendation Craft:   Synthesizes complete sets of implications into well-syndicated recommendations framed as genuine choices with explicit trade-offs; controls quality and process across the initiative.

- Constructive Challenger:   Challenges   stakeholder   and team assumptions   constructively;   brings   new insights;   is developing   the trust-based relationships that make   challenge   welcome rather than   resisted .

- People Developer:   Coaches team members in a   strengths -based way,   solicits   feedback, and creates the conditions for high performance and team health.

- Communication:   Prepares well-structured documents with minimal guidance; presents well to audiences of all sizes; fosters constructive dialogue and balances asking with telling.

JOB SUMMARY

The Benefits Analyst supports the administration, maintenance, and continuous improvement of health and welfare benefit programs. This role serves as a key partner to employees, HR, Payroll, HRIS, Finance, vendors, and other stakeholders to ensure accurate benefit administration, financial reconciliation, compliance, and a positive employee experience. The analyst identifies opportunities to improve processes, leverage technology, and enhance operational efficiency while supporting the overall goals of the Benefits department.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Benefits Administration & Data Management
- Support day-to-day administration of health and welfare benefit programs.
- Review, validate, and process benefits-related data within Workday and supporting systems.
- Analyze benefits data, identify discrepancies, and coordinate resolutions with Payroll, HRIS, vendors, and employees.

Financial Reconciliation & Vendor Management

- Support vendor funding activities, including Health Savings Account (HSA) contributions and reimbursement account administration.
- Process payment requests and ensure accurate and timely financial reporting and vendor remittance.
- Partner with Accounting, Payroll, and vendors to resolve discrepancies and maintain data integrity.

Employee Support & Issue Resolution
- Respond to employee and HR inquiries regarding benefit programs, eligibility, enrollment, and plan provisions.
- Research, resolve, and escalate complex benefits issues when appropriate.
- Communicate benefits information in a clear, professional, and employee-friendly manner.

Annual Enrollment & Program Delivery
- Support planning, testing, validation, and execution of Annual Enrollment activities.
- Assist with benefit communications and educational materials.
- Participate in post-enrollment audits, reconciliations, and issue resolution activities.

Wellness & Employee Engagement
- Assist with wellness program administration and employee engagement initiatives.
- Coordinate with vendors and internal stakeholders to support program communications, presentations, and promotional activities.

Process Improvement & Technology Enablement
- Identify opportunities to streamline workflows, improve accuracy, and reduce manual effort.
- Leverage available technology solutions, reporting tools, automation capabilities, and AI-powered resources to improve operational effectiveness.

Education

Experience

- Strong understanding of health and welfare benefit plan designs, regulations (ERISA, COBRA, HIPAA, ACA), and industry best practices.
- Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel (intermediate to advanced level for data analysis).
- Experience working with HRIS systems (e.g., Workday, SAP, Oracle) strongly preferred.
- Experience managing vendor relationships, reconciling benefit-related financial data, and analyzing large datasets preferred.
- Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
- Excellent attention to detail and time management.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex benefit information clearly and concisely.
- Ability to work independently as part of a team and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- Demonstrated ability and willingness to leverage technology, automation, and AI-enabled tools to improve process efficiency, data accuracy, reporting, employee communications, and overall service delivery.

Executive Leadership Development

- Create, refine, and quality‑check leadership toolkits, facilitation guides, and participant materials, particularly related to leadership behavior and critical competencies.
- Incorporate organizational context into leadership content to enhance relevance.
- Continuously improve content based on participant feedback, survey data, and peer review.

Change Leadership & Organizational Effectiveness
- Partner with change management leaders to align leadership development with enterprise change initiatives and operational transformations.
- Contribute to conversations on leader readiness, adoption risk, and human factors in system and process change.

Operational & Program Management
- Coordinate logistics for high‑visibility leadership programs (venues, materials, vendors, timelines), including external vendors and production.

- Internal:  HR Business Partners, Talent Management, McKesson Learning & Development, Change Management, Executive Leadership, Practice Leaders
- External:  Faculty, consultants, facilitators, assessment vendors, executive education partners

- Consultative diagnosis
- Executive and physician‑level facilitation
- Leadership assessment interpretation
- Applied organizational behavior & change leadership
- High judgment in ambiguous, politically complex environments
- Strong written synthesis and executive communication

Working Style & Operating Context
- Operates with high autonomy and trust, frequently representing OD and Talent perspectives in senior‑level discussions.
- Balances strategic thinking with hands‑on execution, especially in live leadership programs.
- Works extensively across virtual platforms with periodic in‑person facilitation and travel.

Minimum Job Requirements
- Minimum of 7 years of experience delivering organizational development or leadership development work in a complex organization.
- Demonstrated experience facilitating leadership or team development programs.
- Experience supporting organization or team assessments and translating findings into action.
- Ability to manage multiple initiatives simultaneously and meet deliverables.
- Proficiency with Microsoft PowerPoint, Word, and Excel, including development of executive-facing materials.
- Bachelor’s degree in Organizational Development, Human Resources, Psychology, Business Administration, or related field.

Nice-to-Have Requirements
- Master’s degree in Organizational Development, I/O Psychology, or related field.
- Professional certification such as CPTD or APTD (Association of Talent Development), SHRM-CP or SHRM-SCP (Society of Human Resource Management), PHR or SPHR (HR Certification Institute)
- Experience leveraging AI-enabled tools for learning design, organizational analysis, or workforce insights, in alignment with responsible AI standards.
- Experience in healthcare or decentralized operating environments.
- Exposure to change management approaches or certifications (e.g., Prosci).
- Experience using leadership or assessment tools such as Hogan, DISC, SDI, or similar.

We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. À propos du poste

McKesson est à la recherche d’un(e) Directeur(trice), Gouvernance des données stratégique et expérimenté(e) pour diriger les programmes de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise afin d’améliorer la qualité des données, la conformité réglementaire, la confiance des parties prenantes et l’excellence opérationnelle. Cette personne définira et mettra en œuvre des stratégies de gouvernance couvrant la gouvernance des données, la gestion des métadonnées, le catalogage des données, la qualité des données, la gestion des données maîtres (MDM) et les capacités de traçabilité des données (data lineage).

Le ou la titulaire collaborera étroitement avec les équipes d’affaires, technologiques, de gestion des risques, de conformité et de données afin d’établir des cadres de gouvernance, des normes, des politiques et des contrôles soutenant la prise de décisions fondée sur les données et le respect des exigences réglementaires. Ce rôle requiert une solide combinaison de leadership, d’influence, d’expertise en gestion des données et d’engagement des parties prenantes au sein d’un environnement organisationnel complexe.

Ce que vous ferez
- Diriger la stratégie de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise, y compris le modèle opérationnel, les politiques, les normes et les mécanismes de contrôle.

- Favoriser l’adoption et l’optimisation des plateformes de gouvernance et de catalogage des données.

- Établir et superviser les programmes de qualité des données, de gestion des métadonnées, de gestion des données maîtres et de traçabilité des données.

- Collaborer avec les équipes des Risques, de la Conformité, de la Protection de la vie privée, de la Sécurité et de l’Audit afin d’assurer la conformité réglementaire et la maturité des pratiques de gouvernance.

- Développer des indicateurs de gouvernance, des KPI de santé des données et des rapports destinés à la haute direction.

- Travailler avec les parties prenantes de l’entreprise pour définir la propriété des données, l’intendance (data stewardship), la reddition de comptes et les priorités de gouvernance.

- Diriger des équipes multidisciplinaires responsables d’initiatives d’envergure en gouvernance et en gestion des données.

- Recruter, développer et mobiliser des équipes performantes en favorisant une culture de responsabilité, de collaboration et d’amélioration continue.

Exigences de base
- Plus de 12 ans d’expérience professionnelle en gouvernance des données, gestion des données, architecture des données, analytique, conformité ou dans un domaine connexe, dont au moins 4 ans d’expérience en gestion d’équipes.

- Baccalauréat ou expérience professionnelle équivalente.

- Expérience dans la direction de programmes et de modèles opérationnels de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise.

- Expérience dans l’implantation ou la gestion de plateformes de catalogage, de gestion des métadonnées ou de gouvernance des données.

- Expérience en gestion de la qualité des données, traçabilité des données, intendance des données et contrôles de gouvernance.

- Expérience de collaboration avec des équipes de conformité, de gestion des risques, de protection de la vie privée, d’audit ou de réglementation.

- Capacité démontrée à diriger des initiatives transversales et à influencer des parties prenantes de haut niveau.

- Expérience dans l’élaboration de politiques, de normes, de KPI et de cadres de reddition de comptes en matière de gouvernance.

Compétences et expérience privilégiées
- Maîtrise en gestion de l’information, informatique, administration des affaires, analytique des données ou dans un domaine connexe.

- Expérience dans des secteurs réglementés tels que les soins de santé, les produits pharmaceutiques, les services financiers ou l’assurance.

- Connaissance de plateformes de gouvernance des données telles que Collibra, Alation, Informatica, Microsoft Purview ou des outils similaires.

- Expérience avec les principes DAMA-DMBOK et les cadres de gestion des données d’entreprise.

- Connaissance des règlements en matière de protection des données, des mécanismes de gouvernance et des cadres de gestion des risques.

- Expérience à diriger des initiatives de transformation des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise.

- Excellentes compétences en communication auprès des dirigeants et en gestion du changement organisationnel.

- Certifications pertinentes en gouvernance des données, gestion des données, protection de la vie privée ou technologies infonuagiques.

Déplacements, environnement de travail et exigences physiques
- Capacité à voyager jusqu’à 20 % du temps , selon les besoins de l’entreprise.

- Modalités de travail hybrides ou à distance pouvant être offertes selon les besoins de l’entreprise et la situation géographique.

- Capacité à participer à des réunions virtuelles et en personne et à travailler efficacement dans un environnement soutenu par la technologie.

About the Role

McKesson is seeking a strategic and experienced Director, Data Governance to lead enterprise-wide data governance programs that improve data quality, regulatory compliance, business trust, and operational excellence. Competitive base pay, benefits, bonus program

The McKesson Medical-Surgical Inc. (MMS) Legal Department is seeking an experienced, highly organized Lead Counsel, Securities & Corporate Governance to join its Corporate Governance & Strategic Transactions (CG&ST) pillar.

The role reports to the Managing Principal Counsel, CG&ST. This attorney will provide strategic, practical legal counsel on securities law, corporate governance, SEC reporting, Board and committee matters, shareholder engagement, and public company compliance. The successful candidate will help design and implement scalable governance, disclosure, reporting, and compliance processes as MMS prepares to operate as an independent public company.

What You’ll Do

- Work with Assistant Corporate Secretary to build and continuously improve the governance function, including Board processes, governance policies, governance technology, disclosure controls, and public-company readiness initiatives.
- Assist in the operations of the corporate secretarial function, on an as needed basis
- Participate in development of and execute the company's shareholder engagement strategy, including responding to shareholder inquiries, coordinating governance roadshows, and partnering with Investor Relations, Communications, Executive Compensation, Sustainability, and senior leadership. Serve as a key point of contact with proxy advisory firms, including ISS and Glass Lewis.
- Respond to shareholder inquiries and conduct proactive outreach to key shareholders.  Organize and engage in biannual governance roadshows, coordinating with investor relations, communications, executive compensation, the Chief Counsel, Sustainability and other stakeholders.  Engage with ISS or Glass Lewis as appropriate.
- Participate in development of and execute proxy statement disclosure strategy, coordinating cross-functional stakeholders to prepare, draft, and review governance disclosures, manage shareholder proposals, and oversee responses and "no-action" requests.
- Build processes to monitor, assess, and implement developments relevant to corporate governance, proxy statements and shareholder engagement, including best practices and trend developments.
- Serve as a trusted advisor on a broad range of securities law, corporate governance, and public company matters.
- Design, develop, and deliver training programs and practical guidance for business, finance, legal, and executive stakeholders on securities law, corporate governance, and public company compliance obligations.
- Build and enhance scalable disclosure and reporting processes and serve as the legal lead for SEC reporting, including Forms 10-K, 10-Q, and 8-K, in close partnership with Corporate Financial Reporting and other stakeholders.
- Support the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of disclosure controls, public company compliance programs, and applicable listing compliance processes. Collaborate in the preparation and review of SEC filings and other regulatory disclosures.
- Collaborate with Finance, Accounting, Investor Relations and Communications teams on external communications, such as earnings releases and press releases
- Build and oversee insider trading compliance processes, including trading clearance procedures, Rule 10b5-1 trading plans, equity transaction reviews, and share repurchase activities.
- Build processes to monitor, assess, and implement applicable developments in SEC rules, legal policies and compliance relevant to corporate governance and reporting, and support internal education, policy development, implementation and compliance.

Minimum Requirements

- Juris doctor degree or equivalent
- 7+ years relevant experience practicing as an attorney in public company governance and securities laws
- Admitted to practice before a state bar, with active license in good standing

Critical Skills & Experience

- Knowledge of SEC and stock exchange rules and related considerations, particularly as apply to board composition, director independence, conflicts, related person transactions, and proxy statement disclosures.
- Experience building or enhancing governance, disclosure, and compliance processes.
- Proficiency in communicating with and providing clear, practical counsel to executives, directors, shareholders, business teams, and other stakeholders.
- Efficiency in working both independently and collaboratively, with a record of developing strong working relationships in a matrixed enterprise environment.

About MMS

McKesson Medical-Surgical (MMS), which is expected to become Wellverse in early 2027, is a subsidiary and publicly reported segment of the McKesson Corporation. MMS distributes medical-surgical supplies, pharmaceuticals, diagnostic equipment and supplies, along with other solutions and services to virtually every type of healthcare setting and provider outside of the traditional hospital. These markets – often referred to as Alternate Care or Non-Acute Care – include physician offices, surgery centers, long-term care providers, laboratories, home health and hospice agencies, health systems, government facilities and online marketplaces and retailers.

Alternate Care markets are growing rapidly, and MMS is proud to be a leader in this space. With a team of approximately 8,000 employees, a network of 15 distribution centers and approximately 900 delivery vehicles, we collaborate with more than 2,200 leading manufacturers and serve over 200,000 customer accounts across the U.S. Our catalog includes more than 270,000 SKUs of branded and private-label medical-surgical products – from bandages to specialty pharmaceuticals and COVID-19 tests.

This highly visible role will lead value-realization methodology, investment business case governance, executive reporting, and financial performance transparency across a portfolio of strategic transformation initiatives.

This individual will partner across Finance, Technology, and Business teams to ensure transformation investments deliver measurable outcomes while advancing AI-enabled finance capabilities and executive decision support.

The Senior Financial Analyst Transformation & Value Realization for U.S. Pharmaceutical Distribution (USPD) will report directly to the Sr. Director, Finance (AIM28) and serve as the lead finance individual contributor responsible for AIM28 and other strategic initiatives value-realization methodology, investment business case discipline, and executive-ready financial performance transparency. This role will establish and govern the financial logic that connects program benefit realization to actual P&L impact by product, segment, and customer, ensuring transformation value is measurable, defensible, and integrated with the financial outcomes Business Finance teams own.

This is a high-impact transformation finance role operating at the intersection of enterprise strategy, analytics, technology enablement, and financial governance. The position will act as a recognized Finance expert and trusted advisor to McKesson Technology, Big Bet business leads, Business Finance, and the AIM28 Modernization Office, shaping how value is defined, measured, reported, challenged, and sustained across the transformation lifecycle.

The role requires both strategic advisory capability and hands-on execution. The successful candidate will lead complex, cross-functional finance workstreams without formal people-management responsibility, influence senior stakeholders through rigorous financial analysis, and champion AI-enabled finance workflows using tools such as Microsoft Copilot, Claude, Power BI, Power Automate, and other approved enterprise technologies. This is a lean team; the role is expected to lead through expertise, judgment, and influence while personally advancing critical work.

What You’ll Do

Value-realization methodology & P&L governance
- Establish and govern AIM28 Finance value-realization methodology, including benefit definitions, measurement rules, financial validation standards, and decision-ready reporting logic.

- Lead financial benefit tracing from AIM28 Big Bet-level value claims to actual P&L impact by product, segment, and customer where applicable, ensuring alignment with the books owned by Business Finance teams.

- Serve as the Finance escalation point for complex discrepancies between reported AIM28 value and business-unit financial results, recommending resolution paths and governance improvements.

Strategic business case leadership
- Lead development, refinement, and governance of investment business cases for new and in-flight AIM28 initiatives, partnering with McKesson Technology, Big Bet business leads, Business Finance, and the AIM28 Modernization Office.

- Independently pressure-test assumptions behind proposed investments, including cost, timing, benefit sizing, operational readiness, risk, and confidence of realization before recommendations reach Finance leadership.

- Translate complex technology and business proposals into financial narratives, investment recommendations, and executive decision materials that enable disciplined prioritization and funding decisions.

Transformation analytics, reporting strategy & BIE partnership
- Define AIM28 financial reporting strategy and requirements in partnership with the AIM28 BIE resource, translating value methodology, metric definitions, and governance rules into scalable dashboards and automated reporting.

- Act as the senior finance bridge between Big Bet business teams, Technology, analytics partners, and Finance leadership, ensuring reporting solutions reflect the right financial logic, controls, and decision needs.

- Establish quality-control routines for validating dashboard output, benefit reporting, and executive materials before senior leadership review.

AI-enabled finance transformation & workflow innovation
- Champion practical adoption of enterprise AI assistants and automation tools to improve Finance productivity, business case development, insight generation, reconciliation support, and executive narrative drafting.

- Identify, pilot, and scale AI-enabled workflows for recurring finance activities, including data pulls, reconciliations, variance explanations, initiative tracking, and first-draft leadership materials.

- Partner with Technology and analytics stakeholders to explore AI agents, automation patterns, and governed workflow solutions purpose-built for transformation finance use cases.

Program governance, senior stakeholder influence & execution leadership
- Serve as the lead Finance IC and day-to-day strategic partner to the Sr. Director, Finance (AIM28), driving cross-functional workstreams, decision readiness, action tracking, and executive review preparation.

- Lead Finance support for the MBR cadence, four-gate sign-off process, investment prioritization discussions, and executive presentations with rigorous, well-sourced financial analysis.

- Proactively identify financial, operational, data-quality, and governance risks; recommend mitigation actions; and influence stakeholders to resolve issues before they affect leadership decisions or value commitments.

What You Bring

- Recognized finance transformation expertise. You have deep experience translating enterprise transformation goals into financial methodology, measurable outcomes, governance routines, and executive-ready insights.

- Senior stakeholder influence. You can influence Finance, Technology, business, and transformation leaders through structured analysis, clear recommendations, and credible challenge.

- Advanced business case leadership. You have led business case development for complex investments, challenged assumptions, quantified financial impact, and supported funding or prioritization decisions.

- Practical AI and automation leadership. You use AI assistants and automation tools to improve finance workflows and can identify where governed AI-enabled processes can create measurable productivity or insight gains.

- Comfort partnering with a technical counterpart. You don’t need to code yourself, but you can specify the “what” and the “why” clearly enough for a BIE or data engineer to build the “how.”

- Executive presence and strategic communication. You can frame complex financial issues, defend assumptions, and present clear recommendations to senior Finance and business leadership.

- Lead-level ownership without direct reports. You lead by expertise and influence, driving complex work across teams while personally advancing critical analysis and deliverables.

Technical Skills

- Advanced Excel: financial modeling, sensitivity analysis, and scenario planning.

- Executive tooling: advanced PowerPoint for business-case and executive storytelling.

- BI literacy: working knowledge of Power BI or a similar dashboarding tool, enough to read, question, and validate what a BIE builds, even if you’re not building it yourself.

- AI assistants / LLM-based tools: hands-on, practical experience with enterprise AI assistants (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, Claude) for prompt-based analysis, drafting, and workflow automation.

- Workflow automation: familiarity with low-code tools (e.g., Power Automate) or comparable, and curiosity for AI agent-building.

- P&L fluency: understanding of P&L structure and how benefit or value metrics tie back to product, segment, and customer-level financials.

- Systems exposure: familiarity with ERP/financial systems (e.g., SAP) sufficient to trace data lineage back to source.

Minimum Requirement
Degree or equivalent and typically requires 7+ years of relevant experience.

Education
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent experience. MBA or advanced degree preferred.

Critical Skills
- 7+ years of relevant finance, transformation, analytics, value-realization, FP&A, business case development, or investment governance experience. Fewer years may be considered with a directly relevant Master’s qualification and demonstrated lead-level experience. Experience should include ownership of complex, cross-functional finance workstreams, senior stakeholder influence, and measurable value-delivery accountability.

- 7+ years of demonstrated experience establishing financial benefit-tracking methodology, value-realization frameworks, and governance routines for complex transformation or investment portfolios.

- Proven ability to lead and defend complex business cases with cross-functional technology, business, finance, and transformation stakeholders.

- Experience defining executive reporting strategy and partnering with BI, data, or analytics resources to translate finance methodology into governed dashboards, automated reporting, and recurring leadership insights.

- Hands-on, demonstrable experience using AI assistants (e.g., Copilot, Claude) for real work, able to speak to specific prompting techniques and use cases, not just general awareness.

- Strong executive communication and consultative influencing skills, including experience shaping recommendations for senior Finance, Technology, and business leaders.

- Ability to operate with consultative direction, independently determine the approach to complex objectives, and drive outcomes across a lean, fast-paced transformation environment.

- Track record of navigating ambiguity and delivering independently, without a large supporting team.

- Recognized ability to lead complex projects or workstreams through influence, coordinate significant internal resources, and contribute to long-term transformation goals without formal people-management responsibility.

Additional Skills
- Experience leading transformation finance, value-realization, finance analytics, investment governance, or enterprise initiative performance management in a large, matrixed organization preferred.

- Experience in a transformation, PMO, or value-realization function.

- Exposure to building or piloting AI agents or workflows for finance-specific use cases.

- Healthcare, pharmaceutical distribution, or other regulated-industry finance experience.

- Familiarity with McKesson’s (or a comparable) financial systems and reporting cadence (MBR/QBR).

- Experience mentoring or informally developing junior finance analysts.

- Agile delivery experience and strong documentation habits.

À propos du poste

L’Analyste des opérations financières soutient les activités de facturation fournisseurs, de gestion des comptes clients, d’analyse financière et d’amélioration des processus au sein de l’équipe Finances fournisseurs et clients.

Dans ce rôle, vous serez responsable de la gestion quotidienne des comptes fournisseurs, de la résolution des écarts de facturation et de paiement, de l’exécution des conciliations de comptes ainsi que de la préparation de rapports financiers et opérationnels. Vous collaborerez avec des équipes internes et des fournisseurs externes afin d’améliorer les processus, renforcer les contrôles financiers et contribuer aux initiatives d’automatisation.

Ce poste convient à un professionnel de la finance analytique qui apprécie la résolution de problèmes, l’analyse de données financières et la collaboration dans un environnement dynamique.

Ce que vous ferez

- Gérer les activités de facturation fournisseurs de bout en bout, notamment les factures, crédits, ajustements et documents justificatifs.
- Assurer le suivi des comptes clients fournisseurs et coordonner les activités de recouvrement des soldes en souffrance.
- Enquêter sur les écarts de facturation, les différences de paiement, les déductions et les enjeux liés aux conciliations de comptes.
- Effectuer les activités de fin de mois et de fin de trimestre, y compris les conciliations de comptes, les analyses de vieillissement des créances et les rapports financiers.
- Analyser les comptes fournisseurs et les données financières afin d’identifier les tendances, les risques, les causes fondamentales et les occasions d’amélioration.
- Préparer des indicateurs de performance (KPI), des tableaux de bord et des rapports liés à la facturation, aux comptes clients, aux recouvrements et à la résolution des problèmes.
- Collaborer avec les équipes Finance, Approvisionnement, Données maîtresses, Opérations, Juridique, Conformité et les fournisseurs externes.
- Identifier et mettre en œuvre des améliorations de processus visant à accroître l’efficacité, la précision et l’automatisation.
- Participer à la documentation des processus, aux essais et à la mise en œuvre d’améliorations des systèmes.
- Maintenir les procédures opérationnelles normalisées, les contrôles internes et la documentation des processus.
- Soutenir les exigences d’audit et les contrôles SOX applicables.
- Participer à des projets spéciaux et à des initiatives de partage des connaissances.

Exigences de base

- Diplôme universitaire en comptabilité, finance, administration des affaires, économie ou dans un domaine connexe, ou combinaison équivalente de formation et d’expérience.
- Minimum de 2 années d’expérience pertinente en finance, comptabilité, facturation fournisseurs, comptes clients, opérations de revenus, analyse financière ou domaine connexe.
- Expérience des conciliations de comptes et de la résolution d’écarts de facturation ou de paiement.
- Expérience de l’utilisation de Microsoft Excel pour l’analyse de données financières ou opérationnelles.
- Expérience de collaboration avec des partenaires internes et externes pour résoudre des problèmes liés aux comptes ou aux processus.
- Excellentes habiletés de communication en français et en anglais, à l’oral et à l’écrit.

Expérience et compétences privilégiées

- Expérience en facturation fournisseurs, recouvrement, comptes clients ou opérations financières dans un environnement de services partagés ou une grande organisation.
- Maîtrise avancée de Microsoft Excel, incluant les tableaux croisés dynamiques, les fonctions de recherche, Power Query et l’analyse de grands ensembles de données.
- Expérience avec SAP ou un autre système ERP.
- Expérience avec Power BI, l’automatisation des flux de travail ou d’autres outils de visualisation et d’analyse de données.
- Participation à des projets d’amélioration continue, d’automatisation, de transformation des processus ou d’implantation de systèmes.
- Connaissance des contrôles financiers, des audits et des exigences SOX.
- Excellentes aptitudes analytiques, organisationnelles et de résolution de problèmes.
- Capacité à gérer plusieurs priorités et à influencer des intervenants sans autorité directe

Le.la titulaire de ce poste aura à soutenir de façon quotidienne des clients internes et/ou externes à l’extérieur du Québec et/ou aux États-Unis. Par conséquent, ce poste requiert une maîtrise de l’anglais à l’écrit et à l’oral. Veuillez noter que le nombre de postes dont les tâches requièrent une connaissance de la langue anglaise a été restreint dans la mesure du possible.

About the Role

The Financial Operations Analyst supports vendor billing, accounts receivable, financial analysis, and process improvement activities within Supplier & Customer Finance.
In this role, you will manage vendor accounts, investigate billing and payment discrepancies, complete account reconciliations, and prepare financial and operational reporting. You will work with internal teams and external vendors to resolve issues, strengthen financial controls, and identify opportunities to improve or automate processes.
This position is well suited to an analytical finance professional who is comfortable working with financial data, managing multiple priorities, and collaborating across a large organization.

What You’ll Do

- Manage vendor billing activities, including invoices, credits, adjustments, and supporting documentation.
- Monitor vendor accounts receivable and follow up on overdue balances.
- Investigate and resolve billing discrepancies, deductions, payment differences, and reconciliation issues.
- Support month-end and quarter-end activities, including account reconciliations, aging reviews, and financial reporting.
- Analyze vendor accounts and financial data to identify trends, risks, root causes, and improvement opportunities.
- Prepare dashboards, reports, and recommendations related to billing accuracy, receivables, collections, and issue resolution.
- Partner with Finance, Procurement, Master Data, Operations, Legal, Compliance, external vendors, and other business teams.
- Identify opportunities to simplify workflows, improve accuracy, reduce manual work, and automate recurring activities.
- Document business requirements and support testing and implementation of system or process enhancements.
- Maintain process documentation, standard operating procedures, and internal controls.
- Support audit requirements and applicable SOX controls.
- Participate in cross-functional projects and knowledge-sharing activities.

Basic Requirements

- Degree or equivalent qualification in accounting, finance, business administration, economics, or a related field.
- Typically, 2 or more years of relevant experience in finance, accounting, vendor billing, accounts receivable, revenue operations, financial analysis, or a related area.
- Experience performing account reconciliations and investigating billing or payment discrepancies.
- Experience using Microsoft Excel to analyze financial or operational data.
- Experience working with stakeholders to resolve account or process issues.
- Bilingual proficiency in French and English, written and spoken.

Preferred Skills and Experience

- Experience with vendor billing, collections, accounts receivable, or financial operations in a large corporate or shared-services environment.
- Advanced Excel skills, including PivotTables, lookup functions, Power Query, and large dataset analysis.
- Experience with SAP or another enterprise resource planning system.
- Experience with Power BI, workflow automation, or other reporting and digital tools.
- Experience supporting process improvement, automation, system implementation, or business transformation initiatives.
- Knowledge of financial controls, audit requirements, or SOX controls.
- Strong analytical, organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to manage competing priorities and influence outcomes without direct authority.

Job Summary

The Operations Supervisor is responsible for leading day-to-day warehouse and distribution activities to ensure the safe, compliant, and efficient movement of customer products throughout the facility. This position oversees personnel, workflow execution, inventory control, quality compliance, and service performance across receiving, putaway, replenishment, picking, packing, shipping, and inventory management functions. The supervisor plays a critical leadership role in supporting temperature-controlled Plasma Operations, ensuring product integrity and regulatory compliance while driving a culture of safety, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities
Operational Leadership
- Direct and supervise daily warehouse operations and assigned personnel.
- Plan and prioritize work to meet productivity, quality, inventory, and customer service objectives.
- Monitor workflow, staffing levels, and operational performance throughout the shift.
- Ensure adherence to standard operating procedures (SOPs), work instructions, and regulatory requirements.
- Coordinate cross-functional activities with Quality, Inventory Control, Transportation, Maintenance, and Customer Service teams.
- Lead shift startup meetings, communication huddles, and end-of-shift reviews.

Plasma Operations
- Oversee the receipt, storage, movement, and shipment of blood plasma and plasma-derived products.
- Ensure compliance with all customer requirements, GMP, GDP, FDA, OSHA, and applicable regulatory standards.
- Maintain chain of custody, product traceability, and temperature control requirements.
- Investigate and respond appropriately to product variances, quality events, temperature excursions, and inventory discrepancies.
- Ensure proper handling and documentation of temperature-sensitive biological products.
- Partner with Quality personnel to maintain audit readiness and regulatory compliance.

Safety & Compliance
- Promote a strong safety culture and ensure compliance with all company safety policies and procedures.
- Conduct safety observations, investigations, and corrective actions as needed.
- Ensure associates complete required certifications and annual training.
- Enforce PPE requirements, bloodborne pathogen precautions, and hazardous material handling procedures.
- Lead emergency response efforts for spills, incidents, and environmental or safety concerns.

Team Leadership & Development
- Supervise, coach, and develop warehouse associates and team leads.
- Conduct performance reviews, coaching discussions, and corrective action as required.
- Support hiring, onboarding, training, and employee development efforts.
- Foster a positive, accountable, and high-performance work environment.
- Identify and develop future leaders within the organization.

Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree preferred; or equivalent experience.
- 3+ years of leadership experience in warehouse, distribution, manufacturing, logistics, or supply chain operations.
- Experience leading teams in a regulated environment preferred.
- Strong knowledge of inventory management, material handling, and warehouse operations.
- Ability to analyze operational data and use metrics to drive performance.
- Strong communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
- Proficiency with warehouse management systems (WMS), RF technology, and Microsoft Office applications.

Schedule:
- Current schedules consist of four 10-hour shifts : - Sunday - Wednesday, 7:00 AM start , or
- Wednesday - Saturday, 7:00 AM start

- Schedule and shift assignment are subject to change based on business needs .

Working Conditions:
- Regular work in freezer and ultra-low temperature environments ranging from -20°C to -30°C.
- Exposure to temperature-sensitive biologic products and materials requiring specialized handling procedures.
- Ability to wear required cold-weather gear and personal protective equipment for extended periods while performing essential job functions.

This position serves as a frontline leader responsible for storage, movement, and distribution of temperature-sensitive blood plasma and biologic products. Leaders are responsible for maintaining product integrity and complying with all applicable safety, quality, and regulatory requirements while handling these materials.
